verses.1:1: There was a man from Armathaim Sipha, from Mount Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, son of Jeremeel, son of Elihu, son of Thoke, in Nasib of Ephraim.
verses.1:2: And he had two wives: the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the second was Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no child.
verses.1:3: And the man would go up from days to days from his city, from Armathaim, to worship and to sacrifice to the Lord God Sabaoth at Shiloh. And there Eli and his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests of the Lord.
verses.1:4: And a day came when Elkanah sacrificed, and he gave portions to Peninnah his wife and to her sons;
verses.1:5: and to Hannah he gave one portion, because she had no child, yet Elkanah loved Hannah more than her. And the Lord had closed off what was around her womb,
verses.1:6: because the Lord had not given her a child, according to her affliction and according to the despondency of her affliction; and she was despondent on account of this, because the Lord had shut up what was around her womb, so as not to give her a child.
verses.1:7: So he would do year by year when she went up to the house of the Lord; and she would be despondent and weep, and would not eat.
verses.1:8: And Elkanah her husband said to her, "Hannah." And she said to him, "Here I am, sir." And he said to her, "What is the matter with you that you are weeping? And why are you not eating? And why does your heart strike you? Am I not better to you than ten children?"
verses.1:9: And she rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and stood before the Lord. Now Eli the priest was on the seat by the doorposts of the temple of the Lord.
verses.1:10: And she was deeply distressed in soul, and she prayed to the Lord, speaking, and wept.
verses.1:11: And she vowed a vow to the Lord, saying, "Adonai, Lord, Eloe Sabaoth, if You will indeed look upon the humiliation of Your maidservant, and remember me, and give to Your maidservant male offspring, then I will give him before You as one given until the day of his death; and he will not drink wine or strong drink, and no iron will come up upon his head."
verses.1:12: And it came about, as she continued praying long before the Lord, that Eli the priest watched her mouth.
verses.1:13: Now she was speaking in her heart, and her lips were moving, but her voice was not heard; so Eli considered her a drunken woman.
verses.1:14: And Eli's young attendant said to her, "How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine and go away from the presence of the Lord."
verses.1:15: And Hannah answered and said, "No, sir; I am a woman whose day is hard, and I have not drunk wine or strong drink, but I am pouring out my soul before the Lord.
verses.1:16: Do not regard your maidservant as a wicked daughter, for out of the abundance of my complaint I have continued until now."
verses.1:17: And Eli answered and said to her, "Go in peace; may the God of Israel grant you every request of yours that you have asked from Him."
verses.1:18: And she said, "Your maidservant has found favor in your eyes." And the woman went on her way, and she entered her lodging and ate with her husband and drank, and her face was no longer downcast.
verses.1:19: And they rose early in the morning and worshiped the Lord, and went on their way. And Elkanah entered his house at Armathaim, and knew Hannah his wife, and the Lord remembered her.
verses.1:20: And she conceived, and it came about at the time of the days that she gave birth to a son; and she called his name Samuel and said, "Because I asked for him from the Lord God Sabaoth."
verses.1:21: And the man Elkanah and all his household went up to sacrifice in Shiloh the sacrifice of the days and his vows and all the tithes of his land.
verses.1:22: But Hannah did not go up with him, for she said to her husband, "Until the boy goes up, when I wean him, then he will appear in the presence of the Lord and remain there forever."
verses.1:23: And Elkanah her husband said to her, "Do what is good in your eyes; remain until you wean him; only may the Lord establish what has gone out from your mouth." So the woman remained and nursed her son until she weaned him.
verses.1:24: And she went up with him to Shiloh with a three-year-old bull, and loaves of bread, and an ephah of fine flour, and a skin of wine. And she entered the house of the Lord in Shiloh, and the boy was with them.
verses.1:25: And they came forward before the Lord, and his father slaughtered the sacrifice that he used to offer from days to days to the Lord. And he brought the boy forward and slaughtered the bull; and Hannah, the mother of the boy, came forward to Eli
verses.1:26: and said, "Pardon me, sir; as your soul lives, I am the woman who stood before you, with you, when praying to the Lord.
verses.1:27: For this boy I prayed, and the Lord granted my request that I asked from Him;
verses.1:28: and I also lend him to the Lord all the days that he lives, as a loan to the Lord." And she said,
verses.2:1: "My heart has been made firm in the Lord, my horn has been exalted in my God; my mouth has opened wide against enemies, I have rejoiced in Your salvation.
verses.2:2: For there is no one holy like the Lord, and there is no one righteous like our God; there is no one holy besides You.
verses.2:3: Do not boast and do not speak lofty things; let no arrogant speech come out of your mouth, for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and a God who prepares His deeds.
verses.2:4: The bow of the mighty has grown weak, and the weak have girded themselves with strength.
verses.2:5: Those full of bread have been diminished, and the weak have bypassed the land. For a barren woman has given birth to seven, and the one abundant in children has grown weak.
verses.2:6: The Lord puts to death and brings to life; He brings down to Hades and brings up.
verses.2:7: The Lord makes poor and makes rich; He humbles and lifts high.
verses.2:8: He raises the needy from the earth and lifts up the poor from the dung heap, to seat them with rulers of peoples, assigning to them a throne of glory as an inheritance,
verses.2:9: granting a vow to the one who vows; and He has blessed the years of the righteous. For a man is not mighty by strength:
verses.2:10: the Lord will make His adversary weak; the Lord is holy. Let not the prudent man boast in his prudence, and let not the mighty man boast in his might, and let not the rich man boast in his riches; but rather let him who boasts boast in this: to understand and to know the Lord, and to practice justice and righteousness in the midst of the earth. The Lord went up into the heavens and thundered; He Himself will judge the ends of the earth. And He gives strength to our kings, and He will exalt the horn of His anointed one."
verses.2:11: And she left him there before the Lord and went away to Armathaim; and the boy was ministering in the presence of the Lord before Eli the priest.
verses.2:12: Now the sons of Eli the priest were wicked sons, not knowing the Lord
verses.2:13: or the due of the priest from all the people who sacrificed. And the priest's young attendant would come when the meat was boiled, with a three-pronged meat-fork in his hand,
verses.2:14: and he would thrust it into the large cauldron, or into the bronze kettle, or into the pot; everything that came up on the meat-fork the priest would take for himself. In this manner they used to do to all Israel, to those who came to sacrifice to the Lord in Shiloh.
verses.2:15: And before the fat was offered up in smoke, the priest's young attendant would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, "Give meat to roast for the priest, and I will by no means take boiled meat from you out of the cauldron."
verses.2:16: And the man who was sacrificing would say, "Let the fat first be offered up in smoke as is proper, and take for yourself from all that your soul desires." And he said, "No, for you will give it now; and if not, I will take it by force."
verses.2:17: And the sin of the young men was exceedingly great before the Lord, because they treated the sacrifice of the Lord with contempt.
verses.2:18: And Samuel was ministering before the Lord, a boy girded with an ephod bar.
verses.2:19: And his mother made a little cloak for him, and she would bring it up to him from days to days when she went up with her husband to offer the sacrifice of the days.
verses.2:20: And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, saying, "May the Lord repay you with offspring from this woman in place of the loan that you lent to the Lord." And the man went away to his place.
verses.2:21: And the Lord visited Hannah, and she gave birth to three more sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel grew up before the Lord.
verses.2:22: Now Eli was a very old man, and he heard what his sons were doing to the sons of Israel.
verses.2:23: And he said to them, "Why are you acting according to this thing that I hear from the mouth of all the people of the Lord?
verses.2:24: No, children, for the report that I hear is not good; do not act this way, for the reports that I hear are not good, so that the people do not serve God.
verses.2:25: If a man indeed sins against a man, then they will pray for him to the Lord; but if he sins against the Lord, who will pray for him?" Yet they did not listen to the voice of their father, for the Lord surely desired to destroy them.
verses.2:26: And the boy Samuel went on, and was good both with the Lord and with people.
verses.2:27: And a man of God came to Eli and said, "Thus says the Lord: I indeed revealed Myself to the house of your father, when they were in the land of Egypt as servants to the house of Pharaoh;
verses.2:28: and I chose the house of your father out of all the tribes of Israel to serve as priests to Me, and to go up to My altar and to burn incense and to bear an ephod; and I gave to the house of your father all the fire offerings of the sons of Israel for food.
verses.2:29: And why have you looked upon My incense and at My sacrifice with a shameless eye? And have you honored your sons above Me, to be blessed from the firstfruits of every sacrifice of Israel before Me?
verses.2:30: Therefore thus has the Lord, the God of Israel, said: I said, 'Your house and the house of your father will walk before Me forever.' Yet now, says the Lord, far be it from Me! For on the contrary, those who honor Me I will honor, and the one who despises Me will be dishonored.
verses.2:31: Look, days are coming when I will cut off your offspring and the offspring of the house of your father,
verses.2:32: and there will not be an old man of yours in My house all the days.
verses.2:33: Yet I will not cut off a man from My altar, so that his eyes fail and his soul wastes away; and every survivor of your house will fall by the sword of men.
verses.2:34: And this will be the sign to you that will come upon these two sons of yours, Hophni and Phinehas: in one day both of them will die.
verses.2:35: And I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest, who will do everything that is in My heart and in My soul; and I will build for him a faithful house, and he will walk before My anointed one all the days.
verses.2:36: And it will come about that the survivor in the house will come to bow down to him for an obol of silver, saying, 'Cast me into one of your priestly offices to eat bread.'"
verses.3:1: Now the boy Samuel was ministering to the Lord before Eli the priest. And a word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no distinct vision.
verses.3:2: And it happened on that day that Eli was sitting in his place, and his eyes had begun to grow heavy, and he could not see.
verses.3:3: And before the lamp of God was trimmed, Samuel was sleeping in the temple where the ark of God was.
verses.3:4: And the Lord called, "Samuel, Samuel!" And he said, "Here I am."
verses.3:5: And he ran to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." And he said, "I did not call you; go back, sleep." And he went back and slept.
verses.3:6: And the Lord called again, "Samuel, Samuel!" And he went to Eli a second time and said, "Here I am, for you called me." And he said, "I did not call you; go back, sleep."
verses.3:7: Now Samuel did not yet know God, and a word of the Lord had not yet been revealed to him.
verses.3:8: And the Lord called Samuel again a third time. And he got up and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." Then Eli discerned that the Lord had called the boy.
verses.3:9: And he said, "Go back, sleep, child; and it will be, if He calls you, that you will say, 'Speak, for Your servant is listening.'" And Samuel went and lay down in his place.
verses.3:10: And the Lord came and took His stand, and called him as once and again. And Samuel said, "Speak, for Your servant is listening."
verses.3:11: And the Lord said to Samuel, "Look, I am performing My words in Israel: for everyone who hears them, both of his ears will ring.
verses.3:12: On that day I will raise up against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house; I will begin and I will finish.
verses.3:13: And I have declared to him that I Myself am punishing his house forever for the iniquities of his sons, because his sons were speaking evil of God, and he did not admonish them,
verses.3:14: and not even so. I have sworn to the house of Eli, 'Surely the iniquity of the house of Eli will not be atoned for with incense and with sacrifices forever.'"
verses.3:15: And Samuel lay until morning, and rose early in the morning and opened the doors of the house of the Lord. And Samuel was afraid to report the vision to Eli.
verses.3:16: And Eli said to Samuel, "Samuel, child." And he said, "Here I am."
verses.3:17: And he said, "What is the word that was spoken to you? Please do not hide it from me. May God do so to you if you hide from me a word from all the words that were spoken to you in your ears."
verses.3:18: And Samuel reported all the words and hid nothing from him. And Eli said, "He is the Lord; He will do what is good before Him."
verses.3:19: And Samuel grew up, and the Lord was with him, and none of all his words fell to the ground.
verses.3:20: And all Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was faithful as a prophet to the Lord.
verses.3:21: And the Lord manifested Himself again in Shiloh, for the Lord was revealed to Samuel. And Samuel was trusted to become a prophet to the Lord for all Israel, from one end of the land to the other. Now Eli was very old, and his sons kept going on and on, and their way was evil before the Lord.
verses.4:1: And it happened in those days that foreigners gathered together for battle against Israel; and Israel went out to meet them for battle, and they encamped at Ebenezer, and the foreigners encamped in Aphek.
verses.4:2: And the foreigners drew up in array for battle against Israel; and the battle turned, and the men of Israel were defeated before the foreigners, and four thousand men were struck down in the battle line in the field.
verses.4:3: And the people came into the camp, and the elders of Israel said, "Why has the Lord defeated us today before the foreigners? Let us take the ark of our God from Shiloh, and let it go out from our midst, and it will save you from the hand of our enemies."
verses.4:4: And the people sent to Shiloh, and they carried from there the ark of the Lord who sits on the cherubim. And both of the sons of Eli were with the ark, Hophni and Phinehas.
verses.4:5: And it happened, as the ark of the Lord came into the camp, that all Israel cried out with a loud voice, and the earth resounded.
verses.4:6: And the foreigners heard the cry, and the foreigners said, "What is this great cry in the camp of the Hebrews?" And they knew that the ark of the Lord had come into the camp.
verses.4:7: And the foreigners were afraid and said, "These gods have come to them into the camp! Woe to us! Deliver us, Lord, today, for such a thing has not happened yesterday or the day before.
verses.4:8: Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these strong gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague and in the wilderness.
verses.4:9: Be strong and become men, and fight them."
verses.4:10: And they fought them; and the men of Israel were defeated, and each one fled to his tent. And there was a very great slaughter, and thirty thousand ranks fell from Israel.
verses.4:11: And the ark of God was taken, and both sons of Eli died, Hophni and Phinehas.
verses.4:12: And a Jeminite man ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh on that day, with his clothes torn and earth on his head.
verses.4:13: And he came, and look, Eli was on the seat beside the gate, watching the road, for his heart was distraught concerning the ark of God. And the man entered the city to report, and the city cried out.
verses.4:14: And Eli heard the sound of the outcry and said, "What is the outcry of this sound?" And the man hurried, entered, and reported to Eli.
verses.4:15: Now Eli was ninety years old, and his eyes were fixed, and he could not see. And Eli said to the men who were standing around him, "What is the sound of this uproar?"
verses.4:16: And the man hurried, approached Eli, and said to him, "I am the one who has come from the camp, and I have fled from the battle line today." And he said, "What is the thing that has happened, child?"
verses.4:17: And the young man answered and said, "The men of Israel have fled from before the foreigners, and there has been a great slaughter among the people, and both of your sons have died, and the ark of God was taken."
verses.4:18: And it happened, when he mentioned the ark of God, that he fell backward from the seat beside the gate, and his back was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy. And he had judged Israel twenty years.
verses.4:19: Now his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and about to give birth. And she heard the report that the ark of God had been taken and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, and she wept and gave birth, for her labor pains turned upon her.
verses.4:20: And in her time she was dying. And the women who stood beside her said to her, "Do not be afraid, for you have given birth to a son." And she did not answer, and her heart paid no attention.
verses.4:21: And she named the boy Woe Barchaboth, on account of the ark of God and on account of her father-in-law and on account of her husband.
verses.4:22: And they said, "The glory of Israel has been carried into exile when the ark of the Lord was taken."
verses.5:1: Now the foreigners took the ark of God and brought it from Abenner into Ashdod.
verses.5:2: And the foreigners took the ark of the Lord and brought it into the house of Dagon, and set it beside Dagon.
verses.5:3: And the Ashdodites rose early and entered the house of Dagon, and saw, and look, Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of God. And they raised Dagon up and set him in his place. And the hand of the Lord was heavy upon the Ashdodites, and He tormented them and struck them in their posteriors, Ashdod and its borders.
verses.5:4: And it happened, when they rose early in the morning, that look, Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of the covenant of the Lord; and the head of Dagon and both palms of his hands had been severed upon the front of hamapheth, each of them, and both wrists of his hands had fallen upon the entryway; only the spine of Dagon was left.
verses.5:5: Therefore the priests of Dagon and everyone who enters the house of Dagon do not step on the threshold of the house of Dagon in Ashdod to this day, for they step right over it.
verses.5:6: And the hand of the Lord was heavy upon Ashdod, and He afflicted them, and it broke out upon them into the ships, and in the midst of its countryside mice sprang up; and there was a great confusion of death in the city.
verses.5:7: And the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, and they said, "The ark of God shall not remain with us, for His hand is harsh upon us and upon Dagon our god."
verses.5:8: And they sent and gathered the satraps of the foreigners to themselves and said, "What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" And the Gittites said, "Let the ark of God come over to us." And the ark of God went over to Gath.
verses.5:9: And it happened after it went over, that the hand of the Lord was against the city, a very great turmoil; and He struck the men of the city from small to great, and He struck them in their posteriors. And the Gittites made seats for themselves.
verses.5:10: And they sent away the ark of God to Ashkelon. And it happened, as the ark of God entered Ashkelon, that the Ashkelonites cried out, saying, "Why have you turned back to us the ark of the God of Israel, to put us and our people to death?"
verses.5:11: And they sent out and gathered the satraps of the foreigners and said, "Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it settle in its own place, and it will by no means put us and our people to death." For a very heavy confusion came about in the whole city when the ark of the God of Israel entered there.
verses.5:12: And those who lived and did not die were struck in their posteriors, and the cry of the city went up to heaven.
verses.6:1: And the ark was in the country of the foreigners seven months, and their land swarmed with mice.
verses.6:2: And the foreigners called the priests and the diviners and their enchanters, saying, "What shall we do with the ark of the Lord? Make known to us with what we shall send it to its place."
verses.6:3: And they said, "If you are sending away the ark of the covenant of God, the Lord of Israel, do not send it away empty, but surely repay it for the torment, and then you will be healed, and atonement will be made for you; will not His hand turn away from you?"
verses.6:4: And they said, "What shall we repay to it for the torment?" And they said, "According to the number of the satraps of the foreigners, five golden seats, for a calamity is among you and your rulers and the people;
verses.6:5: and golden mice, a likeness of your mice that are destroying the land. And you shall give glory to the Lord, so that He may lighten His hand from you and from your gods and from your land.
verses.6:6: And why do you make your hearts heavy, as Egypt and Pharaoh made their heart heavy? When He mocked them, did they not send them away, and they departed?
verses.6:7: And now take and make a new cart and two cows that have borne their first young, without their young; and yoke the cows to the cart, and lead the young home, away from behind them.
verses.6:8: And you shall take the ark and put it on the cart, and the golden articles you shall repay to it for the torment, and you shall not put them in a berechthan box at its side; and you shall send it away and drive it off, and you shall depart.
verses.6:9: And you shall watch: if it goes on the way to its territory toward Beth-shemesh, He has done this great evil to us; and if not, then we will know that it is not His hand that has touched us, but this has happened to us as a coincidence."
verses.6:10: And the foreigners did so, and they took two cows that had borne their first young and yoked them to the cart, and they kept their young back at home.
verses.6:11: And they put the ark on the cart, and the ergab box and the golden mice.
verses.6:12: And the cows went straight on the way toward the way of Beth-shemesh; on one path they went and grew weary, and they did not turn aside to the right or to the left; and the satraps of the foreigners went after it as far as the borders of Beth-shemesh.
verses.6:13: And those in Beth-shemesh were reaping a wheat harvest in a valley, and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark of the Lord, and they rejoiced to meet it.
verses.6:14: And the cart entered the field of Hoshea, the one in Beth-shemesh, and they set up a great stone there beside it; and they split the wood of the cart, and offered up the cows as a whole burnt offering to the Lord.
verses.6:15: And the Levites brought up the ark of the Lord and the ergab box with it and the golden articles upon it, and they put them on the great stone; and the men of Beth-shemesh offered up whole burnt offerings and sacrifices on that day to the Lord.
verses.6:16: And the five satraps of the foreigners were watching, and they returned to Ashkelon on that day.
verses.6:17: And these are the golden seats which the foreigners repaid for the torment to the Lord: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one.
verses.6:18: And the golden mice were according to the number of all the cities of the foreigners of the five satraps, from a fortified city even to a village of the Perizzite, and as far as the great stone upon which they placed the ark of the covenant of the Lord, which is in the field of Hoshea the Beth-shemite.
verses.6:19: And the sons of Jeconiah were not pleased among the men of Beth-shemesh because they saw the ark of the Lord; and He struck among them seventy men and fifty thousand men. And the people mourned, because the Lord struck among the people a very great blow.
verses.6:20: And the men from Beth-shemesh said, "Who will be able to pass before this holy one? And to whom shall the ark of the Lord go up from us?"
verses.6:21: And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, "The foreigners have returned the ark of the Lord; come down and bring it up to yourselves."
verses.7:1: And the men of Kiriath-jearim came and brought up the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and they brought it into the house of Amminadab, the one on the hill; and they consecrated Eleazar his son to guard the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
verses.7:2: And it came about from the day the ark was in Kiriath-jearim that the days multiplied, and they became twenty years; and all the house of Israel gazed after the Lord.
verses.7:3: And Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, "If with all your heart you are returning to the Lord, remove foreign gods from your midst, and the groves, and prepare your hearts toward the Lord and serve Him alone; and He will deliver you from the hand of the foreigners."
verses.7:4: And the sons of Israel removed the Baals and the groves of Ashtaroth, and they served the Lord alone.
verses.7:5: And Samuel said, "Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray for you to the Lord."
verses.7:6: And they assembled at Mizpah, and they drew water and poured it out before the Lord upon the ground; and they fasted on that day and said, "We have sinned before the Lord." And Samuel judged the sons of Israel at Mizpah.
verses.7:7: And the foreigners heard that all the sons of Israel had gathered together to Mizpah, and the satraps of the foreigners went up against Israel; and the sons of Israel heard, and they were afraid before the foreigners.
verses.7:8: And the sons of Israel said to Samuel, "Do not keep silent away from us so as not to cry out to the Lord your God, and He will save us from the hand of the foreigners."
verses.7:9: And Samuel took one nursing lamb and offered it up as a whole burnt offering with all the people to the Lord; and Samuel cried out to the Lord for Israel, and the Lord heard him.
verses.7:10: And Samuel was offering up the whole burnt offering, and the foreigners were drawing near for battle against Israel; and the Lord thundered with a great voice on that day against the foreigners, and they were thrown into confusion and were defeated before Israel.
verses.7:11: And the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the foreigners, and they struck them as far as below Beth-car.
verses.7:12: And Samuel took one stone and set it up between Mizpah and the Old, and he called its name Ebenezer, Stone of the Helper, and said, "Up to here the Lord has helped us."
verses.7:13: And the Lord humbled the foreigners, and they did not come anymore into the territory of Israel; and the hand of the Lord was against the foreigners all the days of Samuel.
verses.7:14: And the cities which the foreigners had taken from the sons of Israel were restored, and they restored them to Israel from Ashkelon to Azob, and they took back the territory of Israel from the hand of the foreigners; and there was peace between Israel and the Amorite.
verses.7:15: And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
verses.7:16: And he went year by year and made a circuit of Bethel and Gilgal and Mizpah, and he judged Israel in all these consecrated places.
verses.7:17: And his return was to Armathaim, for his house was there; and he judged Israel there, and he built an altar there to the Lord.
verses.8:1: And it came about when Samuel grew old that he appointed his sons as judges for Israel.
verses.8:2: And these were the names of his sons: the firstborn was Joel, and the name of the second was Abijah, judges in Beersheba.
verses.8:3: And his sons did not walk in his way, and they turned aside after profit, and they took gifts, and they turned aside judgments.
verses.8:4: And the men of Israel gathered together and came to Armathaim to Samuel,
verses.8:5: and they said to him, "Look, you have grown old, and your sons do not walk in your way; and now appoint over us a king to judge us, just like the rest of the nations."
verses.8:6: And the word was evil in the eyes of Samuel when they said, "Give us a king to judge us." And Samuel prayed to the Lord.
verses.8:7: And the Lord said to Samuel, "Listen to the voice of the people according to whatever they speak to you; for they have not despised you, but rather they have despised Me, so that I should not reign over them.
verses.8:8: According to all the deeds which they have done to Me from the day that I brought them up out of Egypt until this day, and they forsook Me and served other gods, so they are doing to you also.
verses.8:9: And now listen to their voice; only, you shall solemnly warn them, and you shall declare to them the right of the king who will reign over them."
verses.8:10: And Samuel spoke every word of the Lord to the people who were asking for a king from him,
verses.8:11: and he said, "This will be the right of the king who will reign over you: he will take your sons and place them with his chariots and his horsemen, and as runners ahead of his chariots,
verses.8:12: and to appoint them for himself as commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, and to reap his harvest and to gather his vintage, and to make his implements of war and the implements of his chariots.
verses.8:13: And he will take your daughters as perfumers and as cooks and as bakers.
verses.8:14: And he will take your fields and your vineyards and your olive groves, the good ones, and he will give them to his servants.
verses.8:15: And he will tithe your seeds and your vineyards, and he will give to his eunuchs and to his servants.
verses.8:16: And he will take your male servants and your female servants and your herds of cattle and the good things and your donkeys, and he will tithe them for his works,
verses.8:17: and he will tithe your flocks; and you yourselves will be servants to him.
verses.8:18: And you will cry out in that day because of your king whom you chose for yourselves; and the Lord will not hear you in those days, because you yourselves chose a king for yourselves."
verses.8:19: And the people were not willing to listen to Samuel, and they said to him, "No, but rather a king shall be over us,
verses.8:20: and we too will be like all the nations; and our king will judge us, and he will go out before us, and he will fight our battle."
verses.8:21: And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he spoke them into the ears of the Lord.
verses.8:22: And the Lord said to Samuel, "Listen to their voice and enthrone a king for them." And Samuel said to the men of Israel, "Let each one go off to his city."
verses.9:1: Now there was a man from the sons of Benjamin, and his name was Kish, son of Abiel, son of Ared, son of Bachi, son of Aphek, son of a Jeminite man, a mighty man.
verses.9:2: And he had a son, and his name was Saul, of great stature, a good man, and there was no one among the sons of Israel better than he, from the shoulders and upward tall above all the land.
verses.9:3: Now the donkeys of Kish, Saul's father, were lost; and Kish said to Saul his son, "Take with you one of the young servants, and get up and go and search for the donkeys."
verses.9:4: And they passed through the hill country of Ephraim and passed through the land of Selcha, and they did not find them; and they passed through the land of Easakem, and they were not there; and they passed through the land of Jakim, and they did not find them.
verses.9:5: When they came to Siph, Saul said to his young servant who was with him, "Come, and let us turn back, or else my father will give up on the donkeys and worry about us."
verses.9:6: And the young servant said to him, "Look now, there is a man of God in this city, and the man is honored; everything that he speaks will surely come to pass. And now let us go, so that he may tell us our way on which we have gone."
verses.9:7: And Saul said to his young servant who was with him, "And look, we will go, and what shall we bring to the man of God? For the loaves of bread are gone from our containers, and there is nothing more with us to bring to the man of God that belongs to us."
verses.9:8: And the young servant answered Saul again and said, "Look, a quarter of a shekel of silver is found in my hand, and you shall give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way."
verses.9:9: And formerly in Israel each person used to say this when going to inquire of God: "Come, let us go to the seer"; for the people formerly called the prophet "The Seer."
verses.9:10: And Saul said to his young servant, "The word is good; come, and let us go." And they went to the city where the man of God was.
verses.9:11: As they were going up the ascent of the city, they found the young women who had come out to draw water, and they said to them, "Is the seer here?"
verses.9:12: And the young women answered them and said to them, "He is; look, right ahead of you. Now on account of the day he has come to the city, for the people have a sacrifice today in Bama.
verses.9:13: As soon as you enter the city, you will at once find him in the city before he goes up to Bama to eat; for the people will by no means eat until he enters, because he blesses the sacrifice, and after that the guests eat. And now go up, for on account of the day you will find him."
verses.9:14: And they went up to the city. As they were entering into the middle of the city, look, Samuel came out to meet them, to go up to Bama.
verses.9:15: Now the Lord had uncovered Samuel's ear one day before Saul came to him, saying,
verses.9:16: "About this time tomorrow I will send to you a man from Benjamin, and you shall anoint him as ruler over My people Israel, and he will save My people from the hand of foreigners; for I have looked upon the humiliation of My people, because their cry has come to Me."
verses.9:17: And Samuel saw Saul, and the Lord answered him, "Look, the man of whom I spoke to you! This one will rule over My people."
verses.9:18: And Saul approached Samuel in the middle of the city and said, "Please tell me which is the house of the seer."
verses.9:19: And Samuel answered Saul and said, "I am he. Go up ahead of me to Bama and eat with me today, and I will send you away in the morning and tell you all that is in your heart.
verses.9:20: And concerning your donkeys that were lost three days ago today, do not set your heart on them, for they have been found. And for whom are the finest things of Israel? Are they not for you and for the house of your father?"
verses.9:21: And Saul answered and said, "Am I not the son of a Jeminite man, of the small tribe of the family of Israel, and of the least family out of the whole tribe of Benjamin? And why have you spoken to me according to this word?"
verses.9:22: And Samuel took Saul and his young servant and brought them into the guest hall, and set a place for them there among the foremost of those who were invited, about seventy men.
verses.9:23: And Samuel said to the cook, "Give me the portion that I gave you, which I told you to set aside with you."
verses.9:24: And the cook boiled the thigh and set it before Saul. And Samuel said to Saul, "Look, here is what is left over; set it before you and eat, for it has been set aside for you for a testimony above the others; tear it off." And Saul ate with Samuel on that day.
verses.9:25: And he went down from Bama into the city; and they spread a bed for Saul on the roof, and he slept.
verses.9:26: And it came about as the dawn was rising that Samuel called Saul on the roof, saying, "Get up, and I will send you away." And Saul got up, and he and Samuel went all the way outside.
verses.9:27: As they were going down to the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, "Tell the young man, and let him pass on ahead of us; and you, stand still for now and hear a word of God."
verses.10:1: And Samuel took the flask of oil and poured it on his head, and kissed him and said to him, "Has not the Lord anointed you as ruler over His people, over Israel? And you will rule over the people of the Lord, and you will save them from the hand of their enemies all around. And this is the sign to you that the Lord has anointed you over His inheritance as ruler:
verses.10:2: When you depart from me today, you will find two men by the tombs of Rachel in the hill country of Benjamin, leaping greatly, and they will say to you, 'The donkeys that you went to search for have been found; and look, your father has shaken off the matter of the donkeys, and has become anxious because of you, saying, "What shall I do about my son?"'
verses.10:3: And you will depart from there and come farther, as far as the oak of Tabor, and you will find there three men going up to God at Bethel, one carrying three young goats, and one carrying three containers of bread, and one carrying a skin of wine;
verses.10:4: and they will ask after your welfare and give you two firstfruits of bread, and you shall take them from their hand.
verses.10:5: And after these things you will enter into the hill of God, where the outpost of the foreigners is; there is Nasib the foreigner. And it will come about when you enter there into the city that you will meet a band of prophets coming down from Bama, and before them a harp and a tambourine and a flute and a lyre, and they will be prophesying;
verses.10:6: and the Spirit of the Lord will leap upon you, and you will prophesy with them, and you will be turned into another man.
verses.10:7: And it will come about when these signs come upon you, do everything that your hand finds, for God is with you.
verses.10:8: And you shall go down ahead of Gilead, and look, I am going down to you to offer up a burnt offering and peace sacrifices. You shall wait seven days until I come to you, and I will make known to you what you shall do."
verses.10:9: And it came about when he turned his shoulder to depart from Samuel that God changed his heart to another; and all the signs came to pass on that day.
verses.10:10: And he came from there to the hill, and look, a band of prophets was opposite him; and the Spirit of God leaped upon him, and he prophesied in the midst of them.
verses.10:11: And it came about that all who knew him yesterday and the day before saw, and look, he was in the midst of the prophets. And the people said, each one to his neighbor, "What is this that has come about for the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.10:12: And one of them answered and said, "And who is his father?" Therefore it became a proverb: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.10:13: And he finished prophesying, and came to the hill.
verses.10:14: And his relative said to him and to his young servant, "Where did you go?" And they said, "To search for the donkeys; and we saw that they were not there, and we went in to Samuel."
verses.10:15: And the relative said to Saul, "Please tell me what Samuel said to you."
verses.10:16: And Saul said to his relative, "He certainly told me that the donkeys have been found." But he did not tell him the matter of the kingdom.
verses.10:17: And Samuel summoned all the people to the Lord at Mizpah,
verses.10:18: and he said to the sons of Israel, "Thus the Lord, the God of Israel, spoke, saying, 'I brought up the sons of Israel out of Egypt, and I delivered you from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and from all the kingdoms that were oppressing you.'
verses.10:19: Yet you today have despised God, who Himself is your Savior from all your evils and your afflictions, and you said, 'No, rather you shall set a king over us.' And now present yourselves before the Lord according to your tribes and according to your families."
verses.10:20: And Samuel brought near all the tribes of Israel, and the tribe of Benjamin was chosen by lot.
verses.10:21: And he brought near the tribe of Benjamin by families, and the family of Matri was chosen by lot; and they brought near the family of Matri by men, and Saul son of Kish was chosen by lot. And he searched for him, and he was not found.
verses.10:22: And Samuel inquired further of the Lord, "Is the man coming here?" And the Lord said, "Look, he has hidden himself among the baggage."
verses.10:23: And he ran and took him from there, and set him in the midst of the people; and he stood tall above all the people from the shoulders and upward.
verses.10:24: And Samuel said to all the people, "Have you seen the one whom the Lord has chosen for Himself, that there is no one like him among all of you?" And all the people recognized him and said, "May the king live!"
verses.10:25: And Samuel spoke to the people the right of the king, and wrote it in a book and placed it before the Lord. And Samuel sent all the people away, and each one departed to his place.
verses.10:26: And Saul departed to his house at Gibeah; and men of might, whose hearts the Lord had touched, went with Saul.
verses.10:27: And pestilent men said, "Who will save us—this one?" And they dishonored him, and did not bring him gifts.
verses.11:1: And it happened about a month later that Nahash the Ammonite went up and encamped against Jabesh-gilead; and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash the Ammonite, "Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you."
verses.11:2: And Nahash the Ammonite said to them, "On this condition I will make a covenant with you: by gouging out every right eye of yours, and I will lay a reproach upon Israel."
verses.11:3: And the men of Jabesh said to him, "Leave us alone for seven days, and we will send messengers into all the territory of Israel; if there is no one to save us, we will come out to you."
verses.11:4: And the messengers came to Gibeah, to Saul, and spoke the words in the ears of the people; and all the people lifted up their voice and wept.
verses.11:5: And look, Saul was coming after the morning from the field; and Saul said, "Why is it that the people are weeping?" And they recounted to him the words of the sons of Jabesh.
verses.11:6: And the Spirit of the Lord leaped upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger burned greatly against them.
verses.11:7: And he took two oxen and cut them in pieces, and sent them into all the territory of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, "Whoever does not go out after Saul and after Samuel, in this way they will do to his oxen." And the dread of the Lord came upon the people of Israel, and they cried out as one man.
verses.11:8: And he mustered them at Abiezek in Bama, every man of Israel, six hundred thousand, and the men of Judah, seventy thousand.
verses.11:9: And he said to the messengers who had come, "Thus you shall say to the men of Jabesh, 'Tomorrow you will have salvation when the sun grows hot.'" And the messengers came to the city and reported to the men of Jabesh, and they rejoiced.
verses.11:10: And the men of Jabesh said to Nahash the Ammonite, "Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you will do to us what is good in your sight."
verses.11:11: And it happened on the next day that Saul arranged the people into three divisions, and they entered the middle of the camp in the morning watch, and they struck the sons of Ammon until the day grew hot. And it came about that those who remained were scattered, and there were not left among them two together.
verses.11:12: And the people said to Samuel, "Who is the one who said that Saul will not reign over us? Hand over the men, and we will put them to death."
verses.11:13: And Samuel said, "No one shall die on this day, for today the Lord has worked salvation in Israel."
verses.11:14: And Samuel spoke to the people, saying, "Let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingdom there."
verses.11:15: And all the people went to Gilgal, and Samuel anointed Saul there as king before the Lord in Gilgal, and he sacrificed there sacrifices and peace offerings before the Lord; and Samuel and all Israel rejoiced exceedingly.
verses.12:1: And Samuel said to all Israel, "Look, I have listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and I have made a king reign over you.
verses.12:2: And now, look, the king walks before you, and I have grown old and will sit, and look, my sons are among you; and look, I have walked before you from youth and until this day.
verses.12:3: Here I am! Testify against me before the Lord and before His anointed: whose calf have I taken, or whose donkey have I taken, or whom among you have I oppressed, or whom have I exploited, or from whose hand have I taken a ransom and a sandal? Testify against me, and I will repay you."
verses.12:4: And they said to Samuel, "You have not wronged us, and you have neither oppressed nor crushed us, and you have taken nothing from the hand of anyone."
verses.12:5: And Samuel said to the people, "The Lord is witness among you, and His anointed is witness today on this day, that you have found nothing in my hand." And they said, "He is witness."
verses.12:6: And Samuel spoke to the people, saying, "The Lord is witness, who made Moses and Aaron, who brought up our fathers out of Egypt.
verses.12:7: And now, take your stand, and I will judge you before the Lord, and I will declare to you all the righteousness of the Lord, the things which He did among you and among your fathers:
verses.12:8: When Jacob and his sons entered into Egypt, and Egypt humbled them, then our fathers cried out to the Lord, and the Lord sent Moses and Aaron, and they brought our fathers out of Egypt, and He settled them in this place.
verses.12:9: And they forgot the Lord their God, and He sold them into the hands of Sisera, commander-in-chief of Jabis king of Hazor, and into the hands of foreigners, and into the hands of the king of Moab, and he fought against them.
verses.12:10: And they cried out to the Lord and said, 'We have sinned, because we have forsaken the Lord and have served the Baals and the groves; and now deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we will serve You.'
verses.12:11: And He sent Jeroboam and Barak and Jephthah and Samuel, and He delivered you from the hand of your enemies all around; and you lived in confidence.
verses.12:12: And you saw that Nahash king of the sons of Ammon came against you, and you said, 'No, rather a king will reign over us.'
verses.12:13: And now, here is the king whom you chose, and look, the Lord has given a king over you.
verses.12:14: If you fear the Lord and serve Him and listen to His voice and do not contend with the mouth of the Lord, and both you and the king who reigns over you are walking after the Lord—
verses.12:15: but if you do not listen to the voice of the Lord and contend with the mouth of the Lord, then the hand of the Lord will be against you and against your king.
verses.12:16: And now, take your stand and see this great thing which the Lord will do before your eyes.
verses.12:17: Is it not wheat harvest today? I will call upon the Lord, and He will give thunder and rain; and know and see that your wickedness is great, which you have done before the Lord by asking for a king for yourselves."
verses.12:18: And Samuel called upon the Lord, and the Lord gave thunder and rain on that day; and all the people feared the Lord greatly, and Samuel.
verses.12:19: And all the people said to Samuel, "Pray for your servants to the Lord your God, so that we will not die; for we have added wickedness to all our sins by asking for a king for ourselves."
verses.12:20: And Samuel said to the people, "Do not be afraid; you have done all this wickedness, yet do not turn aside from following the Lord, and serve the Lord with all your heart;
verses.12:21: and do not turn away after those that are nothing, who will accomplish nothing and who will not deliver, because they are nothing.
verses.12:22: For the Lord will not cast off His people because of His great name, because the Lord graciously took you to Himself as a people.
verses.12:23: And as for me, far be it from me to sin against the Lord by ceasing to pray for you; and I will serve the Lord, and I will show you the good and straight way.
verses.12:24: Only fear the Lord and serve Him in truth and with all your heart, for you have seen what great things He has done with you;
verses.12:25: and if in wickedness you do wickedly, both you and your king will be added."
verses.13:2: And Saul chose for himself three thousand men from the men of Israel; and two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel; one thousand were with Jonathan in Geba of Benjamin; and the remainder of the people he sent away, each one to his tent.
verses.13:3: And Jonathan struck Nasib the foreigner who was on the hill, and the foreigners heard; and Saul blew a trumpet throughout all the land, saying, "The servants have rebelled."
verses.13:4: And all Israel heard people saying, "Saul has struck Nasib the foreigner," and Israel was put to shame among the foreigners; and the sons of Israel went up after Saul at Gilgal.
verses.13:5: And the foreigners gathered for war against Israel, and thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen and people like the sand beside the sea in multitude came up against Israel; and they came up and encamped at Michmash, opposite Beth-horon to the rear.
verses.13:6: And the men of Israel saw that they were hard pressed so that they could not advance, and the people hid in the caves and in the sheepfolds and in the rocks and in the pits and in the cisterns.
verses.13:7: And those crossing over crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead; and Saul was still in Gilgal, and all the people were terrified behind him.
verses.13:8: And he waited seven days for the testimony, as Samuel had said; and Samuel did not arrive at Gilgal, and his people were scattered from him.
verses.13:9: And Saul said, "Draw near so that I may offer a burnt offering and peace offerings." And he offered up the burnt offering.
verses.13:10: And it happened as he finished offering up the burnt offering, that Samuel arrived; and Saul went out to meet him to bless him.
verses.13:11: And Samuel said, "What have you done?" And Saul said, "Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and you did not arrive as you directed at the testimony of the days, and the foreigners were gathered at Michmash,
verses.13:12: and I said, 'Now the foreigners will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not implored the face of the Lord.' And I forced myself and offered up the burnt offering."
verses.13:13: And Samuel said to Saul, "You have acted foolishly, because you have not kept my command which the Lord commanded you; for now the Lord had established your kingdom forever over Israel.
verses.13:14: And now your kingdom will not stand; and the Lord will seek for Himself a man according to His heart, and the Lord will command him to be ruler over His people, because you have not kept what the Lord commanded you."
verses.13:15: And Samuel rose and went away from Gilgal on his way; and the remainder of the people went up after Saul to the encounter, following the fighting people. When they arrived from Gilgal at Gibeah of Benjamin, Saul mustered the people who were found with him, about six hundred men.
verses.13:16: And Saul and Jonathan his son and the people and those who were found with them sat in Geba of Benjamin and wept, while the foreigners had encamped at Michmash.
verses.13:17: And a destroyer went out from the field of foreigners in three companies: one company facing the road of Ophrah toward Shual,
verses.13:18: and one company facing the road of Beth-horon, and one company facing the road of Geba that looks down toward Gai of Samin.
verses.13:19: And no worker of iron was found in all the land of Israel, because the foreigners said, "Let the Hebrews not make a sword and a spear."
verses.13:20: And all Israel went down to the land of foreigners to forge each one his reaping hook and the implement, and each one his axe and his sickle.
verses.13:21: And the vintage was ready for reaping; and the implements were three shekels per tooth, and for the axe and for the sickle the setting was the same.
verses.13:22: And it came about in the days of the battle of Michmash, that a sword and a spear were not found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and with Jonathan, yet they were found with Saul and with Jonathan his son.
verses.13:23: And he went out from the outpost of the foreigners, the one on the other side of Michmash; and he did not tell his father.
verses.14:1: And a day came, and Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man carrying his armor, "Come, and let us cross over to Messab of the foreigners, the one on that other side." And he did not tell his father.
verses.14:2: And Saul was sitting on the edge of the hill under the pomegranate tree that was from Magon, and about six hundred men were with him.
verses.14:3: And Ahijah son of Ahitub, brother of Jochabel son of Phinehas son of Levi, priest of God in Shiloh, was carrying an ephod; and the people did not know that Jonathan had gone.
verses.14:4: And in the middle of the pass where Jonathan was seeking to cross over to the outpost of the foreigners, there was a crag of rock on one side and a crag of rock on the other side, and a tooth of rock on this side; the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other was Sennaar.
verses.14:5: The one way was from the north as one comes to Michmash, and the other way was from the south as one comes to Geba.
verses.14:6: And Jonathan said to the young man carrying his armor, "Come, let us cross over to Messaph of these uncircumcised ones, if perhaps the Lord might do something for us; for there is no hindrance for the Lord to save by many or by few."
verses.14:7: And the one carrying his armor said to him, "Do all that your heart inclines to; look, I am with you; as your heart is, so is my heart."
verses.14:8: And Jonathan said, "Look, we are crossing over to the men and will roll down to them.
verses.14:9: If they say this to us, 'Stand back there until we tell you,' then we will stand in our own place and will by no means go up against them.
verses.14:10: And if they say this to us, 'Come up to us,' then we will go up, because the Lord has delivered them into our hands; this will be the sign for us."
verses.14:11: And both of them entered into Messaph of the foreigners. And the foreigners said, "Look, the Hebrews are coming out of their holes where they hid themselves."
verses.14:12: And the men of Messaph answered Jonathan and the one carrying his armor and said, "Come up to us, and we will make a matter known to you." And Jonathan said to the one carrying his armor, "Go up behind me, for the Lord has delivered them into the hands of Israel."
verses.14:13: And Jonathan went up on his hands and on his feet, and the one carrying his armor was with him; and they looked toward the face of Jonathan, and he struck them, and the one carrying his armor was pressing on behind him.
verses.14:14: And the first blow that Jonathan and the one carrying his armor struck was about twenty men, with darts and pebbles of the field.
verses.14:15: And there came to be panic in the camp and in the field, and all the people, those in Messaph and the destroyers, were panic-stricken, and they themselves were unwilling to act; and the earth was terrified, and there came to be panic from the Lord.
verses.14:16: And the watchmen of Saul in Geba of Benjamin looked, and see, the camp was thrown into turmoil on this side and on that.
verses.14:17: And Saul said to the people who were with him, "Count now and see who has gone from among you." And they counted, and look, Jonathan and the one carrying his armor were not found.
verses.14:18: And Saul said to Ahijah, "Bring near the ephod," for he carried the ephod on that day before Israel.
verses.14:19: And it happened while Saul was speaking to the priest that the noise in the camp of the foreigners kept going on continually and increasing. And Saul said to the priest, "Withdraw your hands."
verses.14:20: And Saul and all the people who were with him went up and came as far as the battle; and look, each man's sword was against his neighbor, a very great confusion.
verses.14:21: And the servants who had been with the foreigners yesterday and the day before, who had gone up into the camp, they also turned around to be with Israel, those who were with Saul and Jonathan.
verses.14:22: And all Israel who were hiding in Mount Ephraim also heard that foreigners had fled, and they also joined in behind them into battle.
verses.14:23: And the Lord saved Israel on that day; and the battle passed through Bamoth, and all the people with Saul were about ten thousand men, and the battle was spread out to every city in Mount Ephraim.
verses.14:24: And Saul acted in great ignorance on that day, and he laid a curse on the people, saying, "Cursed is the man who eats bread until evening, and I will take vengeance on my enemy." And none of the people tasted bread.
verses.14:25: And all the land was dining. And Jaal was a forest of an apiary across the face of the field.
verses.14:26: And the people entered into the apiary, and look, they went along speaking; and look, there was no one bringing his hand back to his mouth, because the people feared the oath of the Lord.
verses.14:27: And Jonathan had not heard when his father put the people under oath; and he stretched out the tip of his staff that was in his hand and dipped it into the comb of honey, and brought his hand back to his mouth, and his eyes saw again.
verses.14:28: And one of the people answered and said, "Your father strictly put the people under oath, saying, 'Cursed is the man who eats bread today.'" And the people became faint.
verses.14:29: And Jonathan knew and said, "My father has done away with the land. See how my eyes have seen, because I tasted a little of this honey.
verses.14:30: Rather, if the people had freely eaten today from the spoils of their enemies which they found, then now the blow among the foreigners would have been greater."
verses.14:31: And on that day he struck some of the foreigners in Michmash, and the people grew very weary.
verses.14:32: And the people turned aside to the spoils; and the people took flocks and herds and young of cattle, and slaughtered them on the ground; and the people were eating with the blood.
verses.14:33: And it was reported to Saul, saying, "The people have sinned against the Lord by eating with the blood." And Saul said, "In Gittaim, roll a large stone here to me."
verses.14:34: And Saul said, "Disperse among the people and tell them each to bring here his calf and each his own sheep, and let him slaughter it on this, and you will by no means sin against the Lord by eating with the blood." And all the people brought, each one what was in his hand, and they slaughtered them there.
verses.14:35: And Saul built an altar to the Lord there; this Saul began to build as an altar to the Lord.
verses.14:36: And Saul said, "Let us go down after the foreigners during the night and plunder among them until day dawns, and let us not leave a man among them." And they said, "Do all that is good before you." And the priest said, "Let us draw near here to God."
verses.14:37: And Saul inquired of God, "Shall I go down after the foreigners? Will You deliver them into the hands of Israel?" And He did not answer him on that day.
verses.14:38: And Saul said, "Bring near here all the corners of Israel, and know and see in whom this sin has occurred today.
verses.14:39: For as the Lord lives who saved Israel, if He answers against Jonathan my son, he will surely die." And there was no one answering from all the people.
verses.14:40: And he said to all Israel, "You will be for bondage, and I and Jonathan my son will be for bondage." And the people said to Saul, "Do what is good before you."
verses.14:41: And Saul said, "Lord God of Israel, why is it that You have not answered Your servant today? Is the wrongdoing in me or in Jonathan my son? Lord God of Israel, give clear signs; and if it says this, give now to Your people Israel, give now holiness." And Jonathan and Saul were taken by lot, and the people went out.
verses.14:42: And Saul said, "Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son; the one whom the Lord takes by lot, let him die." And the people said to Saul, "This thing is not to be." And Saul prevailed over the people, and they cast lots between him and Jonathan his son, and Jonathan was taken by lot.
verses.14:43: And Saul said to Jonathan, "Tell me what you have done." And Jonathan told him and said, "I indeed tasted a little honey with the tip of the staff that was in my hand; look, I am to die."
verses.14:44: And Saul said to him, "May God do this to me and add this as well, for you will surely die today."
verses.14:45: And the people said to Saul, "Shall the one who accomplished this great salvation in Israel be put to death today? As the Lord lives, not a hair of his head will fall to the ground, for the people of God acted this day." And the people prayed for Jonathan on that day, and he did not die.
verses.14:46: And Saul went up from behind the foreigners, and the foreigners departed to their own place.
verses.14:47: And Saul obtained by lot to reign; he was allotted the work over Israel. And he fought against all his enemies all around, against Moab and against the sons of Ammon and against the sons of Edom and against Betheor and against the king of Zobah and against the foreigners; wherever he turned, he was saved.
verses.14:48: And he displayed strength, and struck Amalek, and rescued Israel from the hand of those who trampled him.
verses.14:49: And the sons of Saul were Jonathan and Jessiul and Malchishua; and the names of his two daughters: the name of the firstborn was Merab, and the name of the second was Michal.
verses.14:50: And the name of his wife was Ahinoam, daughter of Ahimaaz; and the name of the commander of the army was Abner, son of Ner, son of a relative of Saul.
verses.14:51: And Kish was the father of Saul, and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Jamin, son of Abier.
verses.14:52: And the war against the foreigners was fierce all the days of Saul; and when Saul saw any mighty man and any man who was a son of might, he gathered them to himself.
verses.15:1: And Samuel said to Saul, "The Lord sent me to anoint you as king over Israel, and now listen to the voice of the Lord.
verses.15:2: This is what the Lord Sabaoth said: 'Now I will avenge what Amalek did to Israel, how he met him on the way as he was coming up out of Egypt.
verses.15:3: And now go, and you shall strike Amalek and Jerim and all that belongs to him, and you shall not preserve anything from him, and you shall utterly destroy him; and you shall devote him and all that belongs to him to destruction, and you shall not spare him; and you shall kill from man even to woman, and from young child to nursing infant, and from calf to sheep, and from camel to donkey.'"
verses.15:4: And Saul summoned the people and mustered them in Gilgal: four hundred thousand troops, and Judah thirty thousand troops.
verses.15:5: And Saul came as far as the cities of Amalek and set an ambush in the wadi.
verses.15:6: And Saul said to the Kenite, "Go away and turn aside from the midst of the Amalekite, so that I do not add you along with him, for you showed mercy to the sons of Israel when they were coming up out of Egypt." And the Kenite turned aside from the midst of Amalek.
verses.15:7: And Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as far as Asshur, facing Egypt.
verses.15:8: And he captured Agag king of Amalek alive, and all the people of Jerim he killed with the edge of the sword.
verses.15:9: And Saul and all the people preserved Agag alive, and what was good of the flocks and of the herds and of the provisions and of the vineyards and of all the good things, and he was not willing to utterly destroy them; and every work that was dishonored and despised they utterly destroyed.
verses.15:10: And the word of the Lord came to Samuel, saying,
verses.15:11: "I regret that I made Saul reign as king, because he turned back from following Me and did not keep My words." And Samuel was disheartened, and he cried out to the Lord all night.
verses.15:12: And Samuel rose early and went to meet Israel in the morning; and it was reported to Saul, saying, "Samuel has come to Carmel and has set up a monument for himself." And he turned the chariot around and went down to Gilgal to Saul, and look, he was offering up a whole burnt offering to the Lord, the first of the spoils that he had brought from Amalek.
verses.15:13: And Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, "Blessed are you by the Lord; I have carried out all that the Lord spoke."
verses.15:14: And Samuel said, "And what is the sound of this flock in my ears, and the sound of the cattle that I hear?"
verses.15:15: And Saul said, "I brought them from Amalek, those which the people preserved, the finest of the flock and of the cattle, so that they might be sacrificed to the Lord your God; and the rest I utterly destroyed."
verses.15:16: And Samuel said to Saul, "Stop, and I will report to you what the Lord spoke to me in the night." And he said to him, "Speak."
verses.15:17: And Samuel said to Saul, "Are you not small before Him, leader of a tribe of the family of Israel? And the Lord anointed you as king over Israel.
verses.15:18: And the Lord sent you on a way and said to you, 'Go and utterly destroy; you shall put to death those who sin against Me, Amalek, and you shall make war against them until you make an end of them.'
verses.15:19: And why did you not listen to the voice of the Lord, but rushed to fall upon the spoils and did what is evil before the Lord?"
verses.15:20: And Saul said to Samuel, "Because I listened to the voice of the people; and I went on the way on which the Lord sent me, and I brought Agag king of Amalek, and I utterly destroyed Amalek.
verses.15:21: And the people took from the spoils flocks and herds, the first of what was to be utterly destroyed, before the Lord our God in Gilgal."
verses.15:22: And Samuel said, "Are whole burnt offerings and sacrifices as desired by the Lord as listening to the voice of the Lord? Look, listening is better than a good sacrifice, and paying heed is better than the fat of rams.
verses.15:23: For divination is a sin; pain and toil bring on healing. Because you rejected the word of the Lord, the Lord will also reject you from being king over Israel."
verses.15:24: And Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned, because I transgressed the word of the Lord and your word, because I feared the people and listened to their voice.
verses.15:25: And now, please take away my sin and return with me, and I will worship the Lord your God."
verses.15:26: And Samuel said to Saul, "I am not returning with you, because you rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord will reject you from being king over Israel."
verses.15:27: And Samuel turned his face to go away, and Saul seized the hem of his cloak and tore it.
verses.15:28: And Samuel said to him, "The Lord has torn your kingdom from Israel out of your hand today, and He will give it to your neighbor who is better than you;
verses.15:29: and Israel will be divided in two, and He will not turn back nor change His mind, for He Himself is not like a man to change His mind."
verses.15:30: And Saul said, "I have sinned, yet please honor me before the elders of Israel and before my people, and return with me, and I will worship the Lord your God."
verses.15:31: And Samuel returned after Saul, and he worshiped the Lord.
verses.15:32: And Samuel said, "Bring Agag king of Amalek to me." And Agag came to him trembling. And Agag said, "Is death so bitter?"
verses.15:33: And Samuel said to Agag, "Just as your sword has made women childless, so shall your mother be made childless among women." And Samuel slaughtered Agag before the Lord in Gilgal.
verses.15:34: And Samuel went away to Armathaim; and Saul went up to his house in Gibeah.
verses.15:35: And Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, for Samuel was mourning over Saul; and the Lord regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel.
verses.16:1: And the Lord said to Samuel, "How long will you mourn over Saul, since I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil, and come, I will send you to Jesse, to Bethlehem, for I have seen among his sons one to reign for Me."
verses.16:2: And Samuel said, "How can I go? Saul will hear and kill me." And the Lord said, "Take a heifer from the cattle in your hand and say, 'I have come to sacrifice to the Lord.'
verses.16:3: And you shall invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you shall do, and you shall anoint the one whom I tell you."
verses.16:4: And Samuel did everything that the Lord spoke to him, and came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the city were alarmed at meeting him and said, "Is your coming in peace, seer?"
verses.16:5: And he said, "Peace; I have come to sacrifice to the Lord. Consecrate yourselves and rejoice with me today." And he consecrated Jesse and his sons, and invited them to the sacrifice.
verses.16:6: And it happened as they were entering that he saw Eliab and said, "Surely before the Lord is His anointed."
verses.16:7: And the Lord said to Samuel, "Do not look at his appearance nor at the bearing of his height, because I have rejected him; for not as a man looks does God see, because a man looks at the face, but God looks at the heart."
verses.16:8: And Jesse called Amminadab, and he passed before Samuel, and he said, "Neither has God chosen this one."
verses.16:9: And Jesse brought Shammah forward; and he said, "This one also the Lord has not chosen."
verses.16:10: And Jesse brought his seven sons forward before Samuel; and Samuel said, "The Lord has not chosen among these."
verses.16:11: And Samuel said to Jesse, "Are there no more young men?" And he said, "There is still the youngest; look, he is shepherding the flock." And Samuel said to Jesse, "Send and bring him, for we will certainly not recline until he comes."
verses.16:12: And he sent and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with beauty of eyes, and good in appearance to the Lord. And the Lord said to Samuel, "Rise and anoint David, for this one is good."
verses.16:13: And Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers; and the Spirit of the Lord leaped upon David from that day onward; and Samuel rose and went away to Armathaim.
verses.16:14: And the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was choking him.
verses.16:15: And Saul's servants said to him, "Look now, an evil spirit of the Lord is choking you.
verses.16:16: Let your servants speak now before you, and let them seek for our lord a man who knows how to play on a lyre; and it will happen, when an evil spirit is upon you, that he will play on his lyre, and it will be good for you, and he will give you rest."
verses.16:17: And Saul said to his servants, "Please look for a man for me who plays well, and bring him in to me."
verses.16:18: And one of his young men answered and said, "Look, I have seen a son of Jesse, a Bethlehemite, and he knows music, and the man is intelligent, and the man is a warrior, and wise in speech, and a man good in appearance, and the Lord is with him."
verses.16:19: And Saul sent messengers to Jesse, saying, "Send to me your son David, who is with your flock."
verses.16:20: And Jesse took a gomor of loaves of bread and a skin of wine and one kid from the goats, and sent them by the hand of his son David to Saul.
verses.16:21: And David came in to Saul and stood before him; and he loved him greatly, and he became his armor-bearer.
verses.16:22: And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, "Please let David stand before me, for he has found favor in my eyes."
verses.16:23: And it happened, whenever an evil spirit was upon Saul, that David would take the lyre and play with his hand; and Saul would be refreshed, and it would be good for him, and the evil spirit would depart from him.
verses.17:1: And the foreigners gathered their camps for battle, and they gathered at Socoh of Idumea, and they encamped between Socoh and Azekah, Ephermem.
verses.17:2: And Saul and the men of Israel gathered and encamped in the valley; they drew up in array for battle opposite the foreigners.
verses.17:3: And the foreigners stood on the mountain on one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other side, in a circle between them.
verses.17:4: And a mighty man came out from the battle line of the foreigners, Goliath by name, from Gath; his height was four cubits and a span.
verses.17:5: And a helmet was on his head, and he was clothed in a chain-mail breastplate, and the weight of his breastplate was five thousand shekels of bronze and iron;
verses.17:6: and bronze greaves were over his legs, and a bronze shield was between his shoulders;
verses.17:7: and the shaft of his spear was like a weavers' beam, and his spearhead was six hundred shekels of iron; and the one carrying his armor went before him.
verses.17:8: And he stood up and shouted to the battle line of Israel and said to them, "Why do you come out to draw up in array for battle opposite us? Am I not a foreigner, and you Hebrews and Saul? Choose for yourselves a man, and let him come down to me;
verses.17:9: and if he is able to fight against me and if he strikes me down, then we will be servants to you; but if I prevail and strike him down, you will be servants to us and will serve us."
verses.17:10: And the foreigner said, "Look, I have reproached the battle line of Israel today, on this day; give me a man, and the two of us will fight in single combat."
verses.17:11: And Saul and all Israel heard these words of the foreigner, and they were stunned and very afraid.
verses.17:32: And David said to Saul, "Please do not let the heart of my lord sink because of him; your servant will go and fight with this foreigner."
verses.17:33: And Saul said to David, "You will certainly not be able to go against the foreigner to fight with him, for you are a boy, and he is a fighting man from his youth."
verses.17:34: And David said to Saul, "Your servant was shepherding for his father with the flock; and whenever the lion and the bear came and took a sheep from the herd,
verses.17:35: I went out after it and struck it and pulled it out of its mouth; and if it rose up against me, I seized its throat and struck it and put it to death.
verses.17:36: Both the bear and the lion your servant struck, and the uncircumcised foreigner will be like one of them; will I not go and strike him down, and remove reproach from Israel today? For who is this uncircumcised one who has reproached the battle line of the living God?
verses.17:37: The Lord, who rescued me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, He Himself will rescue me from the hand of this uncircumcised foreigner." And Saul said to David, "Go, and the Lord will be with you."
verses.17:38: And Saul put a cloak on David and a bronze helmet around his head,
verses.17:39: and he belted his sword onto David over his cloak; and he grew weary walking once and twice. And David said to Saul, "I will certainly not be able to go in these, for I have no experience." And they removed them from him.
verses.17:40: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose for himself five perfect stones from the stream and put them in the shepherd's pouch that he had for gathering, and his sling was in his hand; and he approached the foreign man.
verses.17:42: And Goliath saw David and disdained him, for he was a boy, and he was ruddy with beauty of eyes.
verses.17:43: And the foreigner said to David, "Am I like a dog, that you come against me with a rod and stones?" And David said, "No, rather worse than a dog." And the foreigner cursed David by his own gods.
verses.17:44: And the foreigner said to David, "Come here to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the sky and to the beasts of the earth."
verses.17:45: And David said to the foreigner, "You come to me with a sword and with a spear and with a shield, and I go to you in the name of the Lord God Sabaoth of the battle line of Israel, which you have reproached today;
verses.17:46: and the Lord will shut you up today into my hand, and I will kill you and remove your head from you, and I will give your limbs and the limbs of the camp of the foreigners on this day to the birds of the sky and to the wild beasts of the earth; and all the earth will know that there is a God in Israel.
verses.17:47: And all this assembly will know that the Lord does not save with sword and spear; for the battle belongs to the Lord, and the Lord will hand you over into our hands."
verses.17:48: And the foreigner rose up and went to meet David.
verses.17:49: And David stretched out his hand into the pouch and took from there one stone, and he slung it and struck the foreigner on his forehead, and the stone penetrated through the helmet into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.
verses.17:51: And David ran and stood over him, and took his sword and put him to death and removed his head; and the foreigners saw that their mighty man was dead, and they fled.
verses.17:52: And the men of Israel and Judah rose up and raised a battle cry, and they pursued after them as far as the entrance of Gath and as far as the gate of Ashkelon; and the wounded of the foreigners fell on the road of the gates, and as far as Gath and as far as Ekron.
verses.17:53: And the men of Israel returned, turning away from behind the foreigners, and they trampled down their camps.
verses.17:54: And David took the head of the foreigner and brought it to Jerusalem, and he placed his equipment in his tent.
verses.18:6: And the dancing women came out to meet David from all the cities of Israel with tambourines and with gladness and with cymbals;
verses.18:7: and the women led the song and said, "Saul has struck down in his thousands, and David in his ten thousands."
verses.18:8: And the matter appeared evil in the eyes of Saul concerning this saying, and he said, "To David they have given the ten thousands, and to me they have given the thousands."
verses.18:9: And Saul was looking suspiciously at David from that day onward.
verses.18:12: And Saul was afraid of David's presence,
verses.18:13: and he removed him from himself and appointed him for himself as commander of a thousand; and he went out and went in before the people.
verses.18:14: And David was acting with understanding in all his ways, and the Lord was with him.
verses.18:15: And Saul saw that he was acting with great understanding, and he was wary of his presence.
