verses.18:16: And all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went in and went out in the presence of the people.
verses.18:20: And Michal the daughter of Saul loved David, and it was reported to Saul, and it was right in his eyes.
verses.18:21: And Saul said, "I will give her to him, and she will become a stumbling block to him." And the hand of the foreigners was upon Saul.
verses.18:22: And Saul commanded his servants, saying, "Speak secretly to David, saying, 'Look, the king delights in you, and all his servants love you; now you, become son-in-law to the king.'"
verses.18:23: And the servants of Saul spoke these words into the ears of David; and David said, "Is it a light thing in your eyes to become son-in-law to a king? And I am a lowly man and not honored."
verses.18:24: And the servants of Saul reported to him according to these words that David spoke.
verses.18:25: And Saul said, "This is what you will say to David, 'The king has no desire for a gift, except a hundred foreskins of foreigners, to take vengeance on enemies of the king.'" Now Saul planned to cast him into the hands of the foreigners.
verses.18:26: And the servants of Saul reported these words to David, and the matter was right in the eyes of David to become son-in-law to the king;
verses.18:27: and David rose up and went, he and his men, and struck down among the foreigners a hundred men, and he brought up their foreskins to the king, and he became son-in-law to the king, and he gave him his daughter Michal as a wife.
verses.18:28: And Saul saw that the Lord was with David and that all Israel loved him,
verses.18:29: and he continued to be wary of David still more.
verses.19:1: And Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants to put David to death.
verses.19:2: And Jonathan, the son of Saul, favored David greatly. And Jonathan reported to David, saying, "Saul is seeking to put you to death. Therefore be on your guard tomorrow morning, and hide yourself and sit in secret.
verses.19:3: And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak about you to my father; and I will see whatever it may be, and I will report to you."
verses.19:4: And Jonathan spoke good things about David to Saul his father, and said to him, "Let not the king sin against your servant David, because he has not sinned against you, and his deeds are very good.
verses.19:5: And he put his life in his hand and struck down the foreigner, and the Lord worked a great deliverance, and all Israel saw and rejoiced. And why are you sinning against innocent blood to put David to death without cause?"
verses.19:6: And Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan, and Saul swore, saying, "As the Lord lives, he shall not die."
verses.19:7: And Jonathan called David and reported to him all these words. And Jonathan brought David in to Saul, and he was before him as yesterday and the third day.
verses.19:8: And the war occurred again against David, and David prevailed and fought the foreigners, and struck a very great blow among them, and they fled from his presence.
verses.19:9: And an evil spirit of God came upon Saul, and he was sleeping in the house, and a spear was in his hand, and David was playing music with his hands.
verses.19:10: And Saul was seeking to strike the spear into David, and David moved aside from the presence of Saul, and he struck the spear into the wall, and David withdrew and escaped.
verses.19:11: And it happened in that night that Saul sent messengers to the house of David to watch him, to put him to death in the morning. And Michal his wife reported to David, saying, "If you do not save your own life this night, tomorrow you will be put to death."
verses.19:12: And Michal let David down through the window, and he went away and fled and escaped.
verses.19:13: And Michal took the cenotaphs and placed them on the bed, and she placed a liver of goats at its head, and covered them with a garment.
verses.19:14: And Saul sent messengers to take David, and they said that he was sick.
verses.19:15: And he sent for David, saying, "Bring him on the bed to me to put him to death."
verses.19:16: And the messengers came, and look, the cenotaphs were on the bed, and a liver of goats was at its head.
verses.19:17: And Saul said to Michal, "Why have you deceived me like this, and sent away my enemy, and he escaped?" And Michal said to Saul, "He himself said, 'Send me away; if not, I will put you to death.'"
verses.19:18: And David fled and escaped, and came to Samuel at Armathaim, and reported to him all that Saul had done to him. And David and Samuel went and stayed in Auath in Ramah.
verses.19:19: And it was reported to Saul, saying, "Look, David is in Auath in Ramah."
verses.19:20: And Saul sent messengers to take David; and they saw the assembly of the prophets, and Samuel was standing appointed over them. And the Spirit of God came upon the messengers of Saul, and they prophesied.
verses.19:21: And it was reported to Saul, and he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And Saul proceeded to send messengers a third time, and they also prophesied.
verses.19:22: And Saul was furious with anger, and he also went to Armathaim, and came as far as the cistern of the threshing floor that is in Sephi, and asked and said, "Where are Samuel and David?" And someone said, "Look, in Auath in Ramah."
verses.19:23: And he went from there to Auath in Ramah, and the Spirit of God came upon him also, and he went along prophesying until he came to Auath in Ramah.
verses.19:24: And he stripped off his garments and prophesied before them, and fell down naked all that day and all the night. Therefore they were saying, "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.20:1: And David fled from Auath in Ramah, and came before Jonathan and said, "What have I done? And what is my wrongdoing, and what have I sinned before your father, that he is seeking my life?"
verses.20:2: And Jonathan said to him, "Far be it from you! You shall certainly not die. Look, my father will certainly not do a small thing and not uncover my ear; and why would my father hide this matter? This is not so."
verses.20:3: And David answered Jonathan and said, "Your father knows very well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he said that Jonathan should not know this, so that he might not be unwilling. But as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, just as he said, it has been filled up between me and death."
verses.20:4: And Jonathan said to David, "What does your soul desire, and what shall I do for you?"
verses.20:5: And David said to Jonathan, "Look now, tomorrow is the new moon, and I will certainly not sit down to eat; and you shall send me away, and I will hide myself in the plain until evening.
verses.20:6: If your father indeed misses me, then you shall say, 'David earnestly asked leave of me to run all the way to Bethlehem his city, because a sacrifice of the days is there for the whole tribe.'
verses.20:7: If he says thus, 'Well,' there is peace for your servant; and if he answers you harshly, know that the evil has been determined by him.
verses.20:8: And you shall show mercy to your servant, because you have brought your servant into a covenant of the Lord with yourself. And if there is wrongdoing in your servant, put me to death yourself; and why do you bring me to your father like this?"
verses.20:9: And Jonathan said, "Far be it from you! For if I certainly know that the evil has been determined by my father to come upon you, and if it is not to your cities, I will report to you."
verses.20:10: And David said to Jonathan, "Who will report to me if your father answers harshly?"
verses.20:11: And Jonathan said to David, "Go and stay in the field." And both of them went out into the field.
verses.20:12: And Jonathan said to David, "The Lord God of Israel knows that I will examine my father about the time on the third day, and look, should there be good concerning David, and I do not send to you into the field,
verses.20:13: may God do thus to Jonathan and add thus; for I will report the evils against you and uncover your ear, and I will send you away, and you shall go in peace, and the Lord will be with you just as He was with my father.
verses.20:14: And indeed, while I am still alive, you shall show mercy to me; and if I certainly die,
verses.20:15: you shall not remove your mercy from my house forever. And if not, when the Lord removes the enemies of David, each one from the face of the earth,
verses.20:16: let the name of Jonathan be found from the house of David; and may the Lord seek out the enemies of David."
verses.20:17: And Jonathan swore yet again to David, because he loved the soul of the one who loved him.
verses.20:18: And Jonathan said, "Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, because your seat will be noticed.
verses.20:19: And you shall stay until the third day and watch, and you shall come to your place where you may hide on the working day, and you shall sit beside that ergab.
verses.20:20: And I will shoot three times with the arrows, sending them out toward Armattarei.
verses.20:21: And look, I am sending the boy, saying, 'Come, find the gouza for me.' If I say to the boy, 'Here is the arrow, on this side of you; take it,' come; for there is peace for you and there is no word of the Lord, as the Lord lives.
verses.20:22: If I say thus to the young man, 'Here is the arrow, beyond you,' go, because the Lord has sent you away.
verses.20:23: And as for the word that I and you have spoken, look, the Lord is a witness between me and you forever."
verses.20:24: And David hid himself in the field, and the new moon came, and the king came to the table to eat.
verses.20:25: And he sat on his seat as once and again, on the seat by the wall, and he preceded Jonathan, and Abner sat at Saul's side, and David's place was noticed.
verses.20:26: And Saul did not speak on that day, because he said, "It is a mishap; he appears not to be clean, because he has not been cleansed."
verses.20:27: And it happened on the day after the new moon, on the second day, that the place of David was noticed. And Saul said to Jonathan his son, "Why is it that the son of Jesse has not come either yesterday or today to the table?"
verses.20:28: And Jonathan answered Saul and said to him, "David asked leave of me to go all the way to Bethlehem his city,
verses.20:29: and he said, 'Please send me away, because we have a sacrifice of the tribe in the city, and my brothers commanded me. And now, if I have found favor in your eyes, let me please slip away and see my brothers.' Therefore he has not come to the table of the king."
verses.20:30: And Saul was greatly furious with anger against Jonathan and said to him, "Son of deserting girls! For do I not know that you are a partner with the son of Jesse to your own shame and to the shame of your mother's uncovering?
verses.20:31: For all the days that the son of Jesse lives on the earth, your kingdom will not be established. Now therefore send and take the young man, for this one is a son of death."
verses.20:32: And Jonathan answered Saul, "Why is he to die? What has he done?"
verses.20:33: And Saul lifted up the spear against Jonathan to put him to death, and Jonathan knew that this evil had been determined by his father, to put David to death.
verses.20:34: And Jonathan leapt up from the table in furious anger, and he did not eat bread on the second day of the month, because his father had determined against him.
verses.20:35: And it happened in the morning that Jonathan went out into the field, just as he had arranged for the testimony of David, and a small boy was with him.
verses.20:36: And he said to the boy, "Run, find for me the arrows with which I am shooting." And the boy ran, and he shot the arrow and made it pass beyond.
verses.20:37: And the boy came as far as the place of the arrow where Jonathan had shot; and Jonathan called out after the young man and said, "There is the arrow, beyond you."
verses.20:38: And Jonathan called out after his boy, saying, "Hurry quickly, and do not stand still." And Jonathan's boy gathered up the arrows to his master.
verses.20:39: And the boy knew nothing, except Jonathan and David.
verses.20:40: And Jonathan gave his weapons to his boy, and said to his boy, "Go, enter into the city."
verses.20:41: And when the boy entered, David arose from the argab and fell on his face and bowed down to him three times; and each kissed his companion, and each wept with his companion to a great completion.
verses.20:42: And Jonathan said, "Go in peace, and as both of us have sworn in the name of the Lord, saying, 'The Lord will be a witness between me and you, and among your offspring forever.'"
verses.21:1: And David rose up and went away, and Jonathan entered the city.
verses.21:2: And David came to Nob, to Abimelech the priest; and Abimelech was startled at meeting him and said to him, "Why is it that you are alone, and no one is with you?"
verses.21:3: And David said to the priest, "The king has commanded me a matter today and said to me, 'Let no one know the matter about which I am sending you and concerning which I have commanded you.' And I have given notice to the young men in the place called God's Faithfulness, Phellani Maemoni.
verses.21:4: And now, are there five loaves of bread under your hand? Give into my hand what is found."
verses.21:5: And the priest answered David and said, "There are no common loaves under my hand; there are only holy loaves. If the young men have been kept from a woman, then they may eat."
verses.21:6: And David answered the priest and said to him, "Indeed, we have abstained from a woman yesterday and the third day; when I went out on a journey, all the young men were purified. And is the journey itself common? Because it will be sanctified today on account of my equipment."
verses.21:7: And Abimelech the priest gave him the loaves of the presentation, because there were no loaves there except the loaves of the presence, which had been removed from the presence of the Lord for warm bread to be set out on the day he took them.
verses.21:8: And one of the young men of Saul was there on that day, detained, Neessaran, before the Lord; and his name was Doeg the Syrian, tending the mules of Saul.
verses.21:9: And David said to Abimelech, "See if there is a spear or a sword here under your hand, because I have not taken my sword and the equipment in my hand, for the king's matter was in haste."
verses.21:10: And the priest said, "Here is the sword of Goliath the foreigner, whom you struck down in the valley of Elah, and it was wrapped in a cloak. If you will take this one, take it for yourself, for there is no other besides this one here." And David said, "Look, there is none like it; give it to me."
verses.21:11: And he gave it to him. And David rose up and fled on that day from the presence of Saul. And David came to Achish king of Gath.
verses.21:12: And the servants of Achish said to him, "Is this not David, the king of the land? Did not the dancing women lead the song for him, saying, 'Saul struck down in his thousands, and David in his ten thousands'?"
verses.21:13: And David placed the words in his heart, and he was greatly afraid before Achish king of Gath.
verses.21:14: And he altered his face before him and put on a pretense on that day, and he was drumming on the doors of the city and staggering on his hands and falling against the doors of the gate, and his saliva was running down onto his beard.
verses.21:15: And Achish said to his servants, "Look, see an epileptic man! Why did you bring him in to me?
verses.21:16: Do I lack epileptics, that you have brought him in to have epileptic fits before me? This man will not enter a house."
verses.22:1: And David departed from there and escaped, and he came to the cave of Adullam; and his brothers and the house of his father heard, and they went down to him there.
verses.22:2: And everyone in distress and everyone in debt and everyone deeply grieved in soul gathered to him, and he was leader over them; and there were about four hundred men with him.
verses.22:3: And David departed from there to Mizpah of Moab, and he said to the king of Moab, "Please let my father and my mother be with you, until I know what God will do for me."
verses.22:4: And he appealed to the face of the king of Moab, and they lived with him all the days while David was in the stronghold.
verses.22:5: And Gad the prophet said to David, "Do not stay in the stronghold; go, and you will come into the land of Judah." And David went, and he came and stayed in the city of Sarik.
verses.22:6: And Saul heard that David and the men who were with him had become known. Now Saul was sitting on the hill below the field in Bama, and the spear was in his hand, and all his servants were standing beside him.
verses.22:7: And Saul said to his servants who were standing beside him, and he said to them, "Listen now, sons of Benjamin! Will the son of Jesse truly give to all of you fields and vineyards, and will he appoint all of you commanders of hundreds and commanders of thousands?
verses.22:8: For all of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who uncovers my ear when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse, and there is no one among you who feels sorrow for me and uncovers my ear, that my son has stirred up my servant against me as an enemy, as it is this day."
verses.22:9: And Doeg the Syrian, who was set over the mules of Saul, answered and said, "I have seen the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Abimelech son of Ahitub the priest;
verses.22:10: and he inquired for him through God, and he gave him provisions, and he gave him the sword of Goliath the foreigner."
verses.22:11: And the king sent to summon Abimelech son of Ahitub and all the sons of his father, the priests who were in Nob; and they all came to the king.
verses.22:12: And Saul said, "Listen now, son of Ahitub." And he said, "Here I am; speak, lord."
verses.22:13: And Saul said to him, "Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, by giving him bread and a sword, and inquiring for him through God, to set him against me as an enemy, as it is this day?"
verses.22:14: And he answered the king and said, "And who among all your servants is as faithful as David, and son-in-law of the king, and commander of every order of yours, and honored in your house?
verses.22:15: Or have I begun today to inquire for him through God? By no means! Let not the king lay a charge against his servant or upon the whole house of his father, for your servant did not know a small or great matter in all these things."
verses.22:16: And King Saul said, "You will surely die, Abimelech, you and all the house of your father."
verses.22:17: And the king said to the runners who were standing by him, "Advance and put to death the priests of the Lord, because their hand is with David, and because they knew that he was fleeing and did not uncover my ear." But the servants of the king were not willing to put forth their hands to sin against the priests of the Lord.
verses.22:18: And the king said to Doeg, "You turn and fall upon the priests." And Doeg the Syrian turned and put to death the priests of the Lord on that day, three hundred and five men, all bearing an ephod.
verses.22:19: And Nob, the city of the priests, he struck by the edge of the sword, from man to woman, from infant to nursing child, and calf and donkey and sheep.
verses.22:20: And one son of Abimelech son of Ahitub escaped, and his name was Abiathar, and he fled after David.
verses.22:21: And Abiathar reported to David that Saul had put to death all the priests of the Lord.
verses.22:22: And David said to Abiathar, "I knew on that day that Doeg the Syrian would surely report to Saul; I am responsible for the lives of the house of your father.
verses.22:23: Stay with me, do not be afraid; for wherever I seek a place for my life, I will also seek one for your life, for you are kept safe with me."
verses.23:1: And it was reported to David, saying, "Look, the foreigners are fighting against Keilah, and they are plundering; they are trampling the threshing floors."
verses.23:2: And David inquired through the Lord, saying, "Should I go and strike these foreigners?" And the Lord said, "Go, and you will strike among these foreigners, and you will strike Keilah."
verses.23:3: And the men of David said to him, "Look, we are afraid here in Judea; and how will it be if we go to Keilah? Will we go into the spoils of the foreigners?"
verses.23:4: And David proceeded to inquire again through the Lord; and the Lord answered him and said to him, "Arise and go down to Keilah, for I am delivering the foreigners into your hands."
verses.23:5: And David and the men who were with him went to Keilah, and he fought against the foreigners; and they fled from his presence, and he led away their livestock, and he struck a great blow among them; and David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
verses.23:6: And it happened, when Abiathar son of Abimelech fled to David, that he went down with David to Keilah, having an ephod in his hand.
verses.23:7: And it was reported to Saul that David had come to Keilah, and Saul said, "God has sold him into my hands, for he has been shut in by entering a city of doors and bars."
verses.23:8: And Saul commanded all the people for war, to go down to Keilah to hem in David and his men.
verses.23:9: And David knew that Saul was not keeping silent about the evil concerning him, and David said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring near the ephod of the Lord."
verses.23:10: And David said, "Lord, God of Israel, Your servant has surely heard that Saul seeks to come against Keilah to destroy the city because of me.
verses.23:11: Will it be shut up? And now, will Saul come down, just as Your servant has heard? Lord, God of Israel, tell Your servant." And the Lord said, "It will be shut up."
verses.23:13: And David and the men who were with him, about four hundred, rose up and went out from Keilah, and they went wherever they went; and it was reported to Saul that David had escaped from Keilah, and he refrained from going out.
verses.23:14: And he stayed in the wilderness in Maserem, in the narrow passes, and he remained in the wilderness on the mountain of Ziph, in the parched land; and Saul was seeking him all the days, but the Lord did not deliver him into his hands.
verses.23:15: And David saw that Saul was coming out to seek David; and David was on the parched mountain, in Kaine of Ziph.
verses.23:16: And Jonathan son of Saul rose up and went to David at Kaine, and he strengthened his hands in the Lord.
verses.23:17: And he said to him, "Do not be afraid, for the hand of Saul my father will by no means find you; and you will reign over Israel, and I will be second to you; and Saul my father knows that it is so."
verses.23:18: And both of them made a covenant before the Lord; and David stayed in Kaine, and Jonathan departed to his house.
verses.23:19: And the Ziphites went up from the parched land to Saul on the hill, saying, "Look, is David not hidden with us in Nessara, in the narrow passes, in Kaine, on the hill of Hachilah, which is on the right of Jeshimon?
verses.23:20: And now, according to all that is in the king's soul for coming down, let him come down to us; they have shut him up into the hands of the king."
verses.23:21: And Saul said to them, "Blessed are you by the Lord, because you have felt sorrow for me.
verses.23:22: Go now and prepare further, and find out his place where his foot will be quickly, there where you said, so that he may not act craftily.
verses.23:23: And see and know, and we will go with you; and it will be, if he is in the land, that I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah."
verses.23:24: And the Ziphites rose up and went ahead of Saul; and David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, westward, on the right of Jeshimon.
verses.23:25: And Saul and his men went to seek him; and they reported to David, and he went down to the rock that is in the wilderness of Maon. And Saul heard, and he pursued after David into the wilderness of Maon.
verses.23:26: And Saul and his men went on this side of the mountain, and David and his men were on that side of the mountain; and David was taking cover to go away from the presence of Saul, and Saul and his men encamped against David and his men to seize them.
verses.23:27: And a messenger came to Saul, saying, "Hurry and come, for the foreigners have attacked the land."
verses.23:28: And Saul turned back from pursuing after David, and he went to meet the foreigners; therefore that place was named the Divided Rock.
verses.24:1: And David rose up from there and stayed in the narrow passes of En-gedi.
verses.24:2: And it happened, when Saul returned from following the foreigners, that it was reported to him, saying, "David is in the wilderness of En-gedi."
verses.24:3: And he took with himself three thousand chosen men from all Israel, and went to seek David and his men in front of Eddaiem.
verses.24:4: And he came to the herds of the flocks that were by the road, and there was a cave there; and Saul went in to prepare himself, and David and his men were sitting farther inside the cave.
verses.24:5: And David's men said to him, "Look, this is the day of which the Lord spoke to you, to deliver your enemy into your hands, and you will do to him as is good in your eyes." And David rose up and secretly removed the corner of Saul's cloak.
verses.24:6: And it happened after these things that David's heart struck him, because he had removed the corner of his cloak.
verses.24:7: And David said to his men, "By no means may it be for me from the Lord that I should do this thing to the anointed of the Lord, to lay my hand against him, because this man is the anointed of the Lord."
verses.24:8: And David persuaded his men with words, and did not allow them to rise up and slaughter Saul. And Saul rose up and went down the road.
verses.24:9: And David rose up after him out of the cave; and David called out after Saul, saying, "Lord king!" And Saul looked back behind him, and David bent down with his face to the ground and bowed in homage to him.
verses.24:10: And David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to the words of the people who say, 'Look, David is seeking your life'?
verses.24:11: Look, on this day your eyes have seen how the Lord delivered you today into my hand in the cave, and I was not willing to kill you, and I spared you and said, 'I will not lay my hand against my lord, because he is the anointed of the Lord.'
verses.24:12: And look, the corner of your cloak is in my hand; I have removed the corner and have not killed you. And know and see today that there is no evil in my hand, nor ungodliness and rebellion, and I have not sinned against you; yet you are binding my life to take it.
verses.24:13: May the Lord judge between me and you, and may the Lord avenge me on you, yet my hand will not be against you;
verses.24:14: just as the ancient proverb says, 'From the lawless will come forth wrongdoing,' and my hand will not be against you.
verses.24:15: And now after whom are you going out, king of Israel? After whom are you pursuing? After a dead dog, and after a single flea.
verses.24:16: May the Lord become judge and arbiter between me and you; may the Lord see and judge my case and vindicate me from your hand."
verses.24:17: And it happened, when David finished speaking these words to Saul, that Saul said, "Is this your voice, child David?" And Saul lifted up his voice and wept.
verses.24:18: And Saul said to David, "You are more righteous than I, because you have repaid me good, whereas I have repaid you evil.
verses.24:19: And you have declared to me today what good things you have done for me, how the Lord shut me up today into your hands and you did not kill me.
verses.24:20: And because if anyone should find his enemy in distress and send him away on a good road, then the Lord will repay him good, just as you have done today.
verses.24:21: And now, look, I know that you will certainly reign as king, and the kingdom of Israel will stand in your hands.
verses.24:22: And now swear to me by the Lord that you will not destroy my offspring after me, and will not wipe out my name from the house of my father."
verses.24:23: And David swore to Saul. And Saul went away to his place, and David and his men went up to the narrow pass of Messara.
verses.25:1: And Samuel died, and all Israel assembled together and mourned for him, and they buried him in his house in Armathaim. And David rose up and went down to the wilderness of Maon.
verses.25:2: And there was a man in Maon, and his flocks were in Carmel. And the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep and one thousand goats; and it happened as he was shearing his flock in Carmel.
verses.25:3: And the name of the man was Nabal, and the name of his wife was Abigail. And his wife was good in understanding and very good in appearance, while the man was harsh and wicked in his practices, and the man was doglike.
verses.25:4: And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal the Carmelite was shearing his flock.
verses.25:5: And David sent ten young men, and said to the young men, "Go up to Carmel and go to Nabal, and ask after his peace in my name,
verses.25:6: and you will say this: 'For the seasons to come, may you be in good health, your house and all that is yours in good health.
verses.25:7: And now, look, I have heard that your shepherds who were with us in the wilderness are now shearing for you, and we did not hinder them, and we did not command them anything all the days while they were in Carmel.
verses.25:8: Ask your young men, and they will report to you. And let your young men find favor in your eyes, because we have come on a good day. Please give whatever your hand finds to your son David.'"
verses.25:9: And the young men came and spoke these words to Nabal and all these sayings in the name of David, and he sprang up,
verses.25:10: and Nabal answered the servants of David and said, "Who is David, and who is the son of Jesse? Today servants have multiplied who depart, each from before his master.
verses.25:11: And should I take my loaves of bread and my wine and my meat that I have slaughtered for those who shear my sheep, and give them to men of whom I do not know where they are from?"
verses.25:12: And David's young men turned back on their way, and returned and came and reported to David according to these words.
verses.25:13: And David said to his men, "Each of you, strap on his sword." And about four hundred men went up after David, and the two hundred stayed with the baggage.
verses.25:14: And one of the young men reported to Abigail, the wife of Nabal, saying, "Look, David sent messengers from the wilderness to bless our master, and he turned away from them.
verses.25:15: And the men were very good to us; they did not hinder us, nor did they command us all the days that we were with them;
verses.25:16: and while we were in the field, they were like a wall around us both night and day, all the days that we were with them shepherding the flock.
verses.25:17: And now know and see what you will do, because evil has been determined against our master and against his house; and he is a pestilent son, and it is not possible to speak to him."
verses.25:18: And Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, and two vessels of wine, and five prepared sheep, and five ephahs of barley meal, and one gomor of raisins, and two hundred fig cakes, and placed them on the donkeys.
verses.25:19: And she said to her young men, "Go on ahead before me, and look, I am coming behind you." And she did not report it to her husband.
verses.25:20: And it happened, as she was riding on the donkey and coming down in the shelter of the mountain, that look, David and his men were coming down to meet her; and she met them.
verses.25:21: And David said, "Perhaps for injustice I have guarded all that is his in the wilderness, and we did not command to take anything from all that is his, yet he has repaid me evil in return for good.
verses.25:22: May God do so to David and add so to it, if I leave of all that belongs to Nabal until morning one who urinates against a wall."
verses.25:23: And Abigail saw David, and hurried and leaped down from the donkey, and fell before David on her face, and bowed in homage to him to the ground
verses.25:24: at his feet, and said, "On me, my lord, be my wrongdoing; please let your maidservant speak into your ears, and listen to the word of your maidservant.
verses.25:25: Please let my lord not set his heart upon this pestilent man, because according to his name, so he is: Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. And I, your maidservant, did not see your young men whom you sent.
verses.25:26: And now, lord, as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, just as the Lord has hindered you from coming into innocent blood and from your hand bringing deliverance for you, now may your enemies and those who seek evil against my lord become like Nabal.
verses.25:27: And now receive the blessing that your maidservant has brought to my lord, and you will give it to the young men who stand beside my lord.
verses.25:28: Please take away the transgression of your maidservant, because the Lord will certainly make for my lord a faithful house, because the Lord fights the battle of my lord, and evil will never be found in you.
verses.25:29: And a man will rise up pursuing you and seeking your soul, and the soul of my lord will be bound up in the bundle of life with the Lord God, and you will sling the soul of your enemies in the middle of the sling.
verses.25:30: And it will be that the Lord will do for my lord all the good things that He has spoken concerning you, and He will appoint you as ruler over Israel.
verses.25:31: And this will not be to you an abomination and a stumbling block to my lord, to shed innocent blood without cause and for the hand of my lord to bring deliverance for himself. And may the Lord do good to my lord, and you will remember your maidservant, to do good to her."
verses.25:32: And David said to Abigail, "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who sent you to meet me.
verses.25:33: And blessed be your conduct, and blessed be you, who have hindered me today on this day from coming into bloodshed and from my hand bringing deliverance for myself.
verses.25:34: Nevertheless, as the Lord God of Israel lives, who hindered me today from harming you, if you had not hurried and come to meet me, then I said, 'Surely there will not be left to Nabal until the light of morning one who urinates against a wall.'"
verses.25:35: And David received from her hand all that she had brought to him, and said to her, "Go up in peace to your house; see, I have listened to your voice and have favored your face."
verses.25:36: And Abigail came to Nabal, and look, he had a king's banquet, and Nabal's heart was glad within him, and he was exceedingly drunk; and she did not report to him a word, small or great, until the light of morning.
verses.25:37: And it happened in the morning, when Nabal sobered up from the wine, that his wife reported these words, and his heart died within him, and he became like a stone.
verses.25:38: And it happened after about ten days that the Lord struck Nabal, and he died.
verses.25:39: And David heard and said, "Blessed be the Lord, who has judged the case of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and has preserved His servant from the hand of evils; and the Lord has returned the evil of Nabal upon his own head." And David sent and spoke concerning Abigail, to take her for himself as a wife.
verses.25:40: And the servants of David came to Abigail at Carmel and spoke to her, saying, "David has sent us to you, to take you for himself as a wife."
verses.25:41: And she rose up and bowed in homage to the ground on her face and said, "Here is your maidservant, to be a servant girl to wash the feet of your servants."
verses.25:42: And Abigail rose up and mounted the donkey, and five young women followed her; and she went after the servants of David, and she became his wife.
verses.25:43: And David took Ahinoam from Israel, and both of them were his wives.
verses.25:44: And Saul gave Michal his daughter, the wife of David, to Palti, the son of Ameis, who was from Romma.
verses.26:1: And the Ziphites came from the parched land to Saul at the hill, saying, "Look, David is hiding with us on the hill of Chelmath, which faces Jeshimon."
verses.26:2: And Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand chosen men from Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
verses.26:3: And Saul encamped on the hill of Hachilah, facing Jeshimon by the road, and David stayed in the wilderness; and David saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.
verses.26:4: And David sent spies, and he learned that Saul had come ready from Keilah.
verses.26:5: And David arose secretly and went into the place where Saul was sleeping, and Abner son of Ner, his commander-in-chief, was there; and Saul was sleeping in a covered wagon, and the people were encamped around him.
verses.26:6: And David answered and said to Abimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, saying, "Who will go in with me to Saul into the camp?" And Abishai said, "I will go in with you."
verses.26:7: And David and Abishai went in among the people by night, and look, Saul was fast asleep in a covered wagon, and his spear was driven into the ground beside his head, and Abner and his people were sleeping around him.
verses.26:8: And Abishai said to David, "Today the Lord has shut up your enemy into your hands; and now let me strike him with the spear to the ground once, and I will not do it to him a second time."
verses.26:9: And David said to Abishai, "Do not humble him, for who will lay his hand on the Lord's anointed and be held guiltless?"
verses.26:10: And David said, "As the Lord lives, surely the Lord will discipline him, or his day will come and he will die, or he will go down into battle and be added;
verses.26:11: by no means may it be for me from the Lord to lay my hand on the Lord's anointed. And now, please take the spear from beside his head and the flask of water, and let us go away by ourselves."
verses.26:12: And David took the spear and the flask of water from beside his head, and they went away by themselves; and there was no one who saw, and there was no one who knew, and there was no one who woke up; all were sleeping, because a stupor from the Lord had fallen upon them.
verses.26:13: And David crossed over to the other side and stood on the top of the mountain at a distance, and there was a long way between them.
verses.26:14: And David called out to the people and spoke to Abner, saying, "Will you not answer, Abner?" And he said, "Who are you who calls?"
verses.26:15: And David said to Abner, "Are you not a man? And who is like you in Israel? And why do you not guard your lord the king? For one of the people came in to destroy the king your lord.
verses.26:16: And this thing that you have done is not good. As the Lord lives, you are sons of death, you who guard the king your lord, the Lord's anointed. And now, see the king's spear and the flask of water: where are the things that were beside his head?"
verses.26:17: And Saul recognized the voice of David and said, "Is this your voice, child, David?" And David said, "Your servant, lord king."
verses.26:18: And he said, "Why is it that the lord pursues after his servant? For what have I sinned, and what wrongdoing has been found in me?
verses.26:19: And now let my lord the king hear the word of his servant: if God incites you against me, may He smell your sacrifice; and if it is sons of men, cursed are they before the Lord, for they have driven me out today from being established in the inheritance of the Lord, saying, 'Go, serve other gods.'
verses.26:20: And now may my blood not fall to the ground opposite the face of the Lord; for the king of Israel has come out to seek my life, just as the night raven pursues in the mountains."
verses.26:21: And Saul said, "I have sinned. Return, child David, for I will not harm you, because my life was precious in your eyes; and on this day I have acted foolishly and have erred very greatly."
verses.26:22: And David answered and said, "Here is the king's spear; let one of the young men cross over and take it.
verses.26:23: And the Lord will repay each one his righteous deeds and his faithfulness, for the Lord delivered you today into my hands, and I was not willing to lay my hand on the Lord's anointed.
verses.26:24: And look, just as your life was magnified on this very day in my eyes, so may my life be magnified before the Lord, and may He shelter me; and He will rescue me from all distress."
verses.26:25: And Saul said to David, "Blessed are you, child; you will both surely act and surely prevail." And David went away to his place, and Saul returned to his way.
verses.27:1: And David said in his heart, saying, "Now one day I will be given over into the hands of Saul, and there is nothing good for me unless I escape to the land of foreigners and Saul ceases from seeking me within all the territory of Israel, and I will escape from his hand."
verses.27:2: And David set out, and the four hundred men with him, to Achish son of Ammach, king of Gath.
verses.27:3: And David lived with Achish, he and his men, each one and his household, and David and both of his wives, Ahinoam the Israelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.27:4: And it was reported to Saul that David had fled to Gath; and he did not continue any longer to seek him.
verses.27:5: And David said to Achish, "If now your servant has found favor in your eyes, please let them give me a place in one of the cities in the country, and I will live there; and why does your servant live in a royal city with you?"
verses.27:6: And on that day he gave him Ziklag; therefore Ziklag belonged to the king of Judea until this day.
verses.27:7: And the number of the days that David lived in the way of the foreigners was four months.
verses.27:8: And David and his men would go up and attack all the Geshurites and the Amalekites; and look, the land was inhabited from the adjoining places, the one from the fortified places of Gelampsour even as far as Egypt.
verses.27:9: And he would strike the land and would not leave man or woman alive; and he would take flocks and herds and donkeys and camels and clothing, and they turned back and came to Achish.
verses.27:10: And Achish said to David, "Whom did you attack today?" And David said to Achish, "Against the south of Judea, and against the south of Jesmega, and against the south of the Kenizzites."
verses.27:11: And I did not leave man or woman alive to bring into Gath, saying, "May they not report to Gath against us, saying, 'This is what David does.'" And this was his rule all the days that David lived in the country of the foreigners.
verses.27:12: And David was greatly trusted by Achish, saying, "He has been utterly shamed among his people, in Israel; and he will be a servant to me forever."
verses.28:1: And it happened in those days that foreigners gathered together in their camps to go out to fight against Israel; and Achish said to David, "You will surely know that you will go out with me to battle, you and your men."
verses.28:2: And David said to Achish, "So now you will know what your servant will do." And Achish said to David, "Thus I will make you chief bodyguard all the days."
verses.28:3: Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Armathaim, in his city. And Saul had removed the mediums and the wizards from the land.
verses.28:4: And the foreigners gathered together and came and encamped at Shunem; and Saul gathered together every man of Israel, and they encamped at Gilboa.
verses.28:5: And Saul saw the camp of the foreigners, and he was afraid, and his heart was greatly terrified.
verses.28:6: And Saul inquired through the Lord, and the Lord did not answer him, either by dreams, or by the manifestations, or by the prophets.
verses.28:7: And Saul said to his servants, "Seek for me a woman who is a medium, and I will go to her and inquire through her." And his servants said to him, "Look, there is a woman who is a medium in Endor."
verses.28:8: And Saul covered himself up and put on other garments, and he went, he and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night, and he said to her, "Please divine for me by the familiar spirit, and bring up for me the one whom I tell you."
verses.28:9: And the woman said to him, "Look now, you know all that Saul has done, how he has utterly destroyed the mediums and the wizards from the land. And why are you ensnaring my life to put it to death?"
verses.28:10: And Saul swore to her, saying, "As the Lord lives, no wrong will come upon you in this matter."
verses.28:11: And the woman said, "Whom shall I bring up for you?" And he said, "Bring up Samuel for me."
verses.28:12: And the woman saw Samuel, and she cried out with a loud voice; and the woman said to Saul, "Why have you deceived me? And you are Saul!"
verses.28:13: And the king said to her, "Do not be afraid; say whom you have seen." And she said to him, "I have seen gods coming up out of the earth."
verses.28:14: And he said to her, "What did you recognize?" And she said to him, "An upright man coming up out of the earth, and he is wrapped in a double cloak." And Saul knew that this was Samuel, and he bowed down upon his face to the ground and paid homage to him.
verses.28:15: And Samuel said, "Why have you disturbed me, that I should come up?" And Saul said, "I am greatly distressed, and the foreigners are fighting against me, and God has departed from me and has not listened to me any longer, either by the hand of the prophets or by dreams; and now I have called you to make known to me what I should do."
verses.28:16: And Samuel said, "Why do you inquire of me, when the Lord has departed from you and has come to be with your neighbor?
verses.28:17: And the Lord has done to you just as the Lord spoke by my hand, and the Lord will tear your kingdom out of your hand and will give it to your neighbor, to David.
verses.28:18: Because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord and did not carry out the fury of His wrath upon Amalek, therefore the Lord has done this thing to you on this day.
verses.28:19: And the Lord will deliver Israel with you into the hands of foreigners, and tomorrow you and your sons with you will fall, and the Lord will give the camp of Israel into the hands of foreigners."
verses.28:20: And Saul hastened and fell as he stood to the ground, and he was greatly afraid because of the words of Samuel; and there was no longer any strength in him, for he had not eaten bread all the day and all that night.
verses.28:21: And the woman came in to Saul and saw that he was greatly agitated; and she said to him, "Look now, your maidservant has listened to your voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and I have listened to the words that you spoke to me.
verses.28:22: And now, please listen to the voice of your maidservant, and I will set before you a morsel of bread, and eat; and there will be strength in you, because you will go on a journey."
verses.28:23: And he was not willing to eat; and his servants and the woman strongly urged him, and he listened to their voice, and he arose from the ground and sat on the seat.
verses.28:24: And the woman had a pasture-fed heifer in the house; and she hurried and slaughtered it, and she took flour and kneaded it and baked unleavened cakes,
verses.28:25: and she brought it before Saul and before his servants; and they ate, and arose and went away that night.
verses.29:1: And the foreigners gathered all their camps to Aphek, and Israel encamped in Aeddon, which is in Israel.
verses.29:2: And the satraps of the foreigners were passing along by hundreds and thousands, and David and his men were passing along at the rear with Achish.
verses.29:3: And the satraps of the foreigners said, "Who are these passing through?" And Achish said to the commanders of the foreigners, "Is this not David, the servant of Saul king of Israel? He has been with us for days, this second year, and I have found nothing in him from the day he defected to me even until this day."
verses.29:4: And the commanders of the foreigners were displeased with him and said to him, "Send the man back to his place where you stationed him, and let him not come with us into the battle, and let him not become a plotter against the camp. And with what will this man be reconciled to his lord? Will it not be with the heads of those men?
verses.29:5: Is this not David, for whom they led the song in dances, saying, 'Saul struck down in his thousands, and David in his ten thousands'?"
verses.29:6: And Achish called David and said to him, "As the Lord lives, you are upright and good in my eyes, and so are your going out and your coming in with me in the camp, and I have found no evil against you from the day you came to me until this present day, and in the eyes of the satraps you are good.
verses.29:7: And now return and go in peace, and you will certainly not do evil in the eyes of the satraps of the foreigners."
verses.29:8: And David said to Achish, "What have I done to you, and what have you found in your servant from the day I was before you even until this day, that I should not come to fight the enemies of my lord the king?"
verses.29:9: And Achish answered David, "I know that you are good in my eyes, but the satraps of the foreigners say, 'He will not come with us into battle.'
verses.29:10: And now rise early in the morning, you and the servants of your lord who have come with you, and go to the place where I stationed you; and do not put a malicious word in your heart, for you are good before me. And rise early on the way, and let it grow light for you, and go."
verses.29:11: And David rose early, he and his men, to depart and guard the land of the foreigners; and the foreigners went up to fight against Israel.
verses.30:1: And it happened, when David and his men entered Keilah on the third day, that Amalek had made a raid against the south and against Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire;
verses.30:2: and as for the women and all that was in it, from small to great, they did not put to death man or woman, but took them captive and went off on their way.
verses.30:3: And David and his men came to the city, and look, it was burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.
verses.30:4: And David and his men lifted up their voice and wept until there was no longer strength in them to weep.
verses.30:5: And both of the wives of David had been taken captive: Ahinoam the Israelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.30:6: And David was greatly distressed, because the people spoke of stoning him, for the soul of all the people was deeply grieved, each one for his sons and for his daughters; but David was strengthened in the Lord his God.
verses.30:7: And David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, "Bring the ephod near."
verses.30:8: And David inquired through the Lord, saying, "Should I pursue after this raiding band? Will I overtake them?" And He said to him, "Pursue, for you will surely overtake and you will surely rescue."
verses.30:9: And David went, he and the four hundred men with him, and they came as far as the brook Besor; and the rest stopped.
verses.30:10: And the rest pursued with four hundred men, while two hundred men stayed behind, who sat across the brook Besor.
verses.30:11: And they found an Egyptian man in a field, and they took him and brought him to David in the field; and they gave him bread and he ate, and they gave him water to drink;
verses.30:12: and they gave him a piece of a fig cake and he ate, and his spirit was restored in him, because he had not eaten bread and had not drunk water for three days and three nights.
verses.30:13: And David said to him, "To whom do you belong, and where are you from?" And the Egyptian young man said, "I am a servant of an Amalekite man, and my master left me behind because I fell ill three days ago today.
verses.30:14: And we made a raid against the south of Cholthei and against the regions of Judea and against Gilboa, and we burned Ziklag with fire."
verses.30:15: And David said to him, "Will you lead me down to this raiding band?" And he said, "Swear now to me by God not to put me to death and not to deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will lead you down to this raiding band."
verses.30:16: And he led him down there, and look, they were spread out over the face of all the land, eating and drinking and celebrating over all the great spoils that they had taken from the land of the foreigners and from the land of Judah.
verses.30:17: And David came upon them and struck them from dawn until evening and on the next day, and not a man of them escaped except four hundred young men who had mounted the camels and fled.
verses.30:18: And David recovered all that the Amalekites had taken, and he rescued both of his wives.
verses.30:19: And nothing was missing to them, from small to great, from the spoils even to sons and daughters and to all that they had taken of theirs; and David brought everything back.
verses.30:20: And he took all the flocks and the herds and drove them ahead of the spoils; and concerning those spoils it was said, "These are the spoils of David."
verses.30:21: And David came to the two hundred men who had grown too faint to go after David, and he had settled them at the brook Beana; and they came out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him, and David drew near to the people, and they asked him about his welfare.
verses.30:22: And every malicious and wicked man of the fighting men who had gone with David answered and said, "Because they did not pursue with us, we will not give them any of the spoils that we rescued, except to each man his wife and his children; let them lead them away and turn back."
verses.30:23: And David said, "You shall not do so, after the Lord has delivered to us and guarded us, and the Lord has delivered the raiding band that came against us into our hands.
verses.30:24: And who will listen to these words of yours? For they are no less than you; for as is the share of the one going down into battle, so shall be the share of the one sitting by the baggage; they shall share alike."
verses.30:25: And it happened from that day onward that it became a statute and an ordinance for Israel until today.
verses.30:26: And David came to Ziklag, and sent some of the spoils to the elders of Judah and to his neighbors, saying, "Look, some of the spoils of the enemies of the Lord,"
verses.30:27: to those in Beth-zur, and to those in Ramah of the south, and to those in Geththor,
verses.30:28: and to those in Aroer, and to those of Ammadei, and to those in Saphei, and to those in Estheie,
verses.30:29: and to those in Gath, and to those in Keimath, and to those in Saphek, and to those in Theimath, and to those in Carmel, and to those in the cities of Israel, and to those in the cities of Kenezei,
verses.30:30: and to those in Jerimuth, and to those in Beersheba, and to those in Noo,
verses.30:31: and to those in Hebron, and to all the places through which David had passed, he and his men.
verses.31:1: And the foreigners were fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled from before the foreigners and fell wounded on Mount Gilboa.
verses.31:2: And the foreigners closed in on Saul and his sons, and the foreigners struck down Jonathan and Jonadab and Malchishua, son of Saul.
verses.31:3: And the battle grew heavy against Saul, and the marksmen, men who were archers, found him, and he was wounded in the abdomen.
verses.31:4: And Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and pierce me through with it, so that these uncircumcised ones do not come and pierce me through and mock me." And his armor-bearer was not willing, because he was greatly afraid; so Saul took the sword and fell upon it.
verses.31:5: And his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, and he also fell upon his sword and died with him.
verses.31:6: And Saul died, and his three sons, and his armor-bearer, on that day together.
verses.31:7: And the men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley and those who were on the other side of the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, and they abandoned their cities and fled; and the foreigners came and lived in them.
verses.31:8: And it happened on the next day that the foreigners came to strip the dead; and they found Saul and his three sons fallen on the mountains of Gilboa.
verses.31:9: And they turned him over and stripped off his armor, and sent it into the land of the foreigners all around, proclaiming good news to their idols and to the people;
verses.31:10: and they placed his armor in the temple of Astarte, and they fastened his body on the wall of Beth-em.
verses.31:11: And the inhabitants of Jabesh of Gilead heard what the foreigners had done to Saul.
verses.31:12: And every man of valor arose and marched all night, and took the body of Saul and the body of Jonathan his son from the wall of Beth-sam, and brought them to Jabesh and burned them there.
verses.31:13: And they took their bones and buried them under the field of Jabesh, and fasted seven days. And it happened after Saul died that David returned from striking Amalek, and David stayed in Ziklag two days.

notes.1:1: The Greek preserves distinct proper names compared to the Hebrew Masoretic Text: Armathaim Sipha (for Ramathaim-zophim, with Armathaim also used in 1:3, 1:19, and 2:11 where the Hebrew has Ramah), Jeremeel (for Jeroham), Thoke (for Tohu), and 'in Nasib of Ephraim' (for 'son of Zuph, an Ephrathite').
notes.1:3: Literally 'from days to days,' a Hebraistic Greek idiom meaning annually ('year by year'); similarly, 'the sacrifice of the days' (1:21; 2:19) refers to the annual sacrifice. 'Sabaoth' is an untranslated transliteration of the Hebrew title meaning 'hosts.'
notes.1:5: The Greek reads 'one portion' (vs. Hebrew 'a double/worthy portion') and in vv. 5-6 attributes Hannah's despondency directly to her childlessness rather than to provocation by Peninnah.
notes.1:11: 'Adonai, Lord, Eloe Sabaoth' preserves the Greek transliteration of Hebrew divine titles ('Lord ... God of hosts'). The Greek literally says 'seed of men' (meaning male offspring), specifies 'until the day of his death' and 'no iron' (vs. Hebrew 'all the days of his life' and 'razor'), and adds the abstention from wine and strong drink.
notes.1:14: The Greek uniquely has 'Eli's young attendant' address Hannah rather than Eli himself, and in 1:15 Hannah literally calls herself a woman 'whose day is hard' (vs. Hebrew 'troubled in spirit').
notes.2:5: The Greek reads 'the weak have bypassed the land' (vs. Hebrew 'the hungry have ceased'), continuing the distinctive Septuagint readings in Hannah's song (see also vv. 2-3 and 8-9).
notes.2:10: The Greek includes a substantial expansion paralleling Jeremiah 9:23-24 ('Let not the prudent man boast...') and concludes with plural 'our kings' (vs. Hebrew 'His king').
notes.2:18: The Greek text reads 'ephod bar,' an untranslated manuscript variant of 'bad' (transliterating the Hebrew word for 'linen'), referring to a linen ephod.
notes.2:22: Like the Dead Sea Scrolls manuscript 4QSam-a, the Greek omits the clause found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text about Eli's sons lying with the women serving at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
notes.2:31: The Greek reads 'your offspring' (reflecting the Hebrew consonant root for 'seed') rather than the Masoretic Text's 'your arm,' and in v. 32 omits the first half of the Hebrew verse while reading 'in My house.'
notes.3:3: Greek "before the lamp of God was trimmed" (prin episkeuasthenai) differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("before the lamp of God had gone out").
notes.3:10: The Septuagint reads "called him as once and again" without repeating the spoken name here, having doubled "Samuel, Samuel" in 3:4 and 3:6; both 3:9 and 3:10 also omit "Lord" from Samuel's reply.
notes.3:13: Greek "speaking evil of God" preserves an ancient reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "bringing a curse on themselves" (one of the traditional scribal corrections).
notes.3:14: Greek "and not even so" (kai oud' houtos) completes the thought of 3:13 (reflecting Hebrew "and not so" rather than "and therefore"); in the oath, Greek ei (literally "if") functions as a Semitic idiom for emphatic negation.
notes.3:21: The Septuagint includes an expanded conclusion describing Samuel's accreditation across all Israel and the ongoing wickedness of Eli's sons, not present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.4:1: Greek allophyloi literally means "foreigners" (people of another tribe), the Septuagint's regular designation for the Philistines throughout 1 Kingdoms.
notes.4:12: Greek Iemeinaios ("Jeminite") reflects the Hebrew gentilic Yemini, a shortened designation for a Benjamite.
notes.4:15: The Septuagint gives Eli's age as ninety years (Hebrew Masoretic Text: ninety-eight) and adds Eli's question to the men standing around him.
notes.4:18: The Septuagint reads "his back was broken" and "twenty years" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "his neck" and "forty years."
notes.4:21: The Septuagint names the child Ouai Barchaboth ("Woe Barchaboth"), corresponding to Hebrew Ichabod ("Where is the glory?").
notes.5:1: The Septuagint reads Abenner here, contrasting with Ebenezer (Greek Abenezer) in 4:1 and in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.5:4: Greek hamapheth is an untranslated transliteration of Hebrew hammiphtan ("the threshold"); the verse also preserves a double rendering of Dagon's severed hands and reads "the spine of Dagon."
notes.5:6: Greek "into the ships" (eis tas naus) and the explicit mention of mice springing up in the countryside are distinctive Septuagint readings not found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.5:9: Greek hedrai means both "posteriors" (anatomical seat) and "seats," producing the Septuagint's striking reading that the afflicted Gittites "made seats for themselves."
notes.5:10: The Septuagint reads Ashkelon and the Ashkelonites where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Ekron and the Ekronites.
notes.6:1: Greek uses 'allophyloi' ('foreigners'), the Septuagint's regular designation throughout 1-2 Kingdoms for the Philistines. The closing clause 'and their land swarmed with mice' is a Septuagint plus not found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.6:4: Greek 'hedras' ('seats') is an anatomical euphemism for the buttocks or posterior, reflecting the affliction of chapter 5 (where the Hebrew has 'tumors'). Likewise, 'for the torment' (Greek 'tes basanou', also in vv. 3, 8, 17) corresponds to the Hebrew term for a guilt offering.
notes.6:8: The Greek text (following Codex Vaticanus) reads the negative 'shall not put' and pairs 'box' with the transliteration 'berechthan' (comparable to 'ergab' in vv. 11 and 15), a double rendering of the Hebrew word for a coffer or chest.
notes.6:14: Greek reads 'Hoshea' (also in v. 18) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Joshua,' and states transitively that they set up a great stone beside it rather than merely noting a stone was there.
notes.6:16: Greek reads 'Ashkelon' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Ekron.'
notes.6:18: Greek renders Hebrew 'unwalled village' as 'a village of the Perizzite' and reads 'the great stone' where the Masoretic Text has 'the great Abel' (or 'meadow').
notes.6:19: The opening clause concerning 'the sons of Jeconiah' is a distinctive Septuagint reading not present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:1: Greek reads 'Amminadab' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Abinadab.'
notes.7:9: Greek reads 'with all the people' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'entirely' (a whole offering).
notes.7:12: Greek reads 'the Old' ('tes palaias', reflecting a Hebrew reading 'Jeshanah') where the Masoretic Text has 'Shen,' and gives both the transliteration 'Ebenezer' and its Greek gloss 'Stone of the Helper.'
notes.7:14: Greek reads 'from Ashkelon to Azob' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'from Ekron to Gath.'
notes.7:16: Greek reads 'in all these consecrated places' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads simply 'in all these places'; in v. 17 (and 8:4) Greek reads 'Armathaim' where the Masoretic Text reads 'Ramah.'
notes.8:3: Greek 'synteleia' can mean 'completion' or, in Hellenistic administrative usage, 'contribution/profit,' corresponding here to Hebrew 'dishonest gain.'
notes.8:12: Greek reads 'commanders of hundreds' (where the Masoretic Text has 'fifties') and 'reap his harvest and gather his vintage' (where the Masoretic Text has 'plow his ground and reap his harvest').
notes.8:16: Greek reads 'your herds of cattle and the good things' (where the Masoretic Text has 'your best young men') and 'he will tithe them for his works' (where the Masoretic Text has 'put them to his work').
notes.8:18: The closing clause 'because you yourselves chose a king for yourselves' and the plural 'in those days' are Septuagint readings not present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.9:1: Greek has the distinct ancestral names Ared, Bachi, and Aphek (for MT Zeror, Becorath, and Aphiah); in 9:2 Greek reads "all the land" rather than "all the people" (compare 10:23).
notes.9:4: Greek preserves the distinct place names Selcha, Easakem, and Jakim (for MT Shalishah, Shaalim, and Yemini), and Siph in 9:5 (for MT Zuph).
notes.9:12: Greek transliterates Hebrew bamah ("high place") as the place name Bama throughout chapters 9-11; "on account of the day" renders dia ten hemeran (also in 9:13).
notes.9:16: "Foreigners" renders Greek allophyloi (lit. "people of another tribe"), the Septuagint's regular designation for the Philistines in 1-2 Kingdoms.
notes.9:24: Following 9:22 ("about seventy men," vs. MT thirty), Greek here reads "boiled," "for a testimony," and "tear it off" (apoknize), and in 9:25 reads "they spread a bed for Saul on the roof, and he slept."
notes.10:1: Greek preserves the longer reading ("over His people, over Israel? And you will rule over the people of the Lord, and you will save them from the hand of their enemies all around. And this is the sign to you..."), omitted in the Masoretic Text by homoioteleuton.
notes.10:2: Greek reads plural "tombs," "in the hill country of Benjamin" (orei, vs. MT "border"), and "leaping greatly" (hallomenous megala, where MT has the place name Zelzah).
notes.10:5: Greek contains a doublet for Hebrew netsiv ("garrison/prefect"), first translating it as "the outpost" (to anastema) and then transliterating it as a personal name, "Nasib the foreigner."
notes.10:8: Greek reads "ahead of Gilead" (Galaad) rather than "before me to Gilgal" (compare Gilgal in 11:14-15).
notes.10:19: Greek renders "tribes" with skeptra (lit. "scepters," also in 9:21; 10:20-21) and "families" with phylas; in 10:24 Greek reads "recognized him" (egnosan) rather than "shouted."
notes.11:1: Greek opens with "about a month later" (hos meta mena, matching 4QSama), whereas the Masoretic Text ends 10:27 with "he kept silent."
notes.11:5: Greek reads "after the morning" (meta to proi), reflecting Hebrew habboqer ("the morning") rather than MT habbaqar ("the oxen").
notes.11:8: Greek preserves the distinct place name Abiezek (for MT Bezek) together with "in Bama," and gives the muster numbers as six hundred thousand for Israel and seventy thousand for Judah (vs. MT three hundred thousand and thirty thousand).
notes.11:13: Greek names Samuel rather than Saul as the speaker here, and in 11:15 likewise attributes the anointing, sacrifices, and rejoicing specifically to Samuel (vs. the people and Saul in MT).
notes.12:2: Greek reads "and will sit" (kathēsomai), taking the Hebrew verb from the root "to sit" rather than "to grow gray-haired" (Masoretic Text).
notes.12:3: Greek reads "a ransom and a sandal" (exilasma kai hypodēma; cf. Sirach 46:19), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "a bribe to blind my eyes with it."
notes.12:9: Greek names "Jabis king of Hazor" (cf. Jabin in Judges 4:2), a phrase absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text; "foreigners" (allophyloi) is the Septuagint's regular term for the Philistines in 1-2 Kingdoms.
notes.12:11: Greek reads the distinct names "Jeroboam and Barak," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Jerubbaal and Bedan."
notes.12:25: Greek reads "will be added" (prostethēsesthe), rendering the Hebrew verb for "be swept away" as if from the root "to add" (likely understood in the sense of being gathered to the dead).
notes.13:3: Greek treats Hebrew netsiv ("garrison" or "prefect") as a proper name, "Nasib," translates Geba as "the hill," and reads "The servants have rebelled" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Let the Hebrews hear." The Greek text omits verse 1, the difficult chronological formula in the Hebrew.
notes.13:5: Greek reads the distinct place name "Beth-horon to the rear," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "east of Beth-aven."
notes.13:15: The Septuagint preserves a longer text here ("on his way; and the remainder of the people... arrived from Gilgal") that is absent from the shorter Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.13:18: Greek reads "Geba" where the Hebrew has "the border," transliterates Hebrew gei ("valley") as the proper name "Gai," and has the distinct name "Samin" where the Hebrew reads "Zeboim."
notes.13:21: This difficult verse diverges sharply from the Hebrew Masoretic Text (which refers to a pim weight): Greek speaks of "the vintage... ready for reaping," "three shekels per tooth," and the same "setting" (hypostasis).
notes.13:23: Greek reads "from the outpost" (ex hypostaseōs), apparently taking the initial letter of Hebrew matsav ("garrison") as the preposition "from," and includes "and he did not tell his father" here rather than in 14:1.
notes.14:1: Messab (spelled Messaph in vv. 6, 11, 12, and 15) transliterates Hebrew matsav ("garrison" or "outpost"). Here and throughout the chapter, "foreigners" translates Greek allophyloi, the Septuagint's standard designation for the Philistines in 1–2 Kingdoms.
notes.14:2: Greek reads "the hill" (where the Masoretic Text has the place name Gibeah) and "Magon" (where the Masoretic Text has Migron).
notes.14:3: Greek reads "Jochabel" and "Levi" where the Masoretic Text has "Ichabod" and "Eli".
notes.14:4: Greek reads "Sennaar" (where the Masoretic Text has Seneh) and preserves a textual doublet describing both "a crag of rock" and "a tooth of rock".
notes.14:18: Greek reads "the ephod" twice where the Masoretic Text reads "the ark of God".
notes.14:23: Greek reads "Bamoth" (where the Masoretic Text has Beth-aven) and includes an expansion describing ten thousand men with Saul and fighting throughout every city of Mount Ephraim.
notes.14:25: Jaal transliterates Hebrew ya'ar ("forest") alongside its Greek translation "forest". Greek also reads "all the land was dining" (and in v. 26 "went along speaking" where Hebrew refers to flowing honey).
notes.14:33: Greek reads the place name "In Gittaim" (En Geththaim) where the Masoretic Text reads "You have acted treacherously".
notes.14:41: Greek preserves a longer prayer of Saul in which "clear signs" (delous) and "holiness" (hosioteta) represent the Urim and Thummim.
notes.14:47: Greek includes the distinct name "Betheor" (Baitheor, absent from the Masoretic Text) and opens with a double clause regarding Saul's allotment to reign and his allotted work.
notes.14:48: The Greek text adds the untranslatable form aunanein after dynamin ("strength"), widely recognized as an ancient scribal duplication of dynamin.
notes.14:49: Greek reads "Jessiul" where the Masoretic Text has "Ishvi".
notes.14:51: Greek reads "son of Jamin, son of Abier" where the Masoretic Text has only "son of Abiel".
notes.15:2: Greek "Sabaoth" transliterates the Hebrew word for "hosts" or "armies."
notes.15:3: Greek "Jerim" (also in 15:8) treats the Hebrew root for "devote to destruction" (herem) as a proper name, alongside a doublet of the command to destroy Amalek.
notes.15:7: Greek reads "Asshur," where the Hebrew text reads "Shur."
notes.15:12: Literally "a hand," a Hebraism for a monument. The Greek also diverges from the Hebrew by making Samuel the subject who came to Carmel and turned the chariot back to Gilgal, and by adding Saul's offering of spoils.
notes.15:23: The Greek differs sharply from the Hebrew here; "healing" (Greek therapeian, also "service" or "care") likely reflects a sound-alike rendering of Hebrew teraphim ("household idols").
notes.15:29: Greek reads "Israel will be divided in two," where the Hebrew text reads "the Glory (or Eternity) of Israel will not lie."
notes.15:34: Greek "Armathaim" (also in 16:13) reflects the dual name Ramathaim, where the Hebrew text reads "Ramah."
notes.16:8: Greek reads "Amminadab" (Ameinadab), where the Hebrew text reads "Abinadab."
notes.16:12: Greek adds "to the Lord," names "David" explicitly, and reads "for this one is good" where the Hebrew text reads "for this is he."
notes.16:14: Greek "was choking" (also "is choking" in 16:15) renders a verb meaning "choke" or "strangle," where the Hebrew text reads "was terrorizing."
notes.16:20: Greek "gomor" (a dry measure corresponding to Hebrew omer or homer) reflects a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants for "donkey" (a donkey laden with bread).
notes.17:1: The Septuagint regularly renders Philistines as allophyloi ("foreigners"), here locates Socoh in "Idumea" (MT: "Judah"), and gives the third place name as "Ephermem" (MT: "at Ephes-dammim").
notes.17:4: The Greek gives Goliath's height as "four cubits and a span" (agreeing with 4QSam^a and Josephus), whereas the Hebrew MT reads "six cubits and a span."
notes.17:8: The Greek reads "Hebrews and Saul" (Hebraioi kai Saoul), differing from the Hebrew MT's "servants of Saul."
notes.17:32: The shorter Septuagint narrative omits 17:12-31, 41, 50, and 55-58, and here reads "the heart of my lord" where the Hebrew MT reads "the heart of a man."
notes.17:52: The Septuagint preserves distinct geographic readings here: "entrance of Gath" (MT: "a valley"), "gate of Ashkelon" (MT: "Ekron"), and "road of the gates" (MT: "Shaaraim").
notes.18:6: The shorter Septuagint text of chapter 18 omits 18:1-5, 10-11, 17-19, and 29b-30, and here has the dancing women come out to meet David rather than King Saul (MT).
notes.18:21: Unlike the Hebrew MT, which places a wish about the Philistines against David inside Saul's speech, the Greek ends Saul's speech after "stumbling block" and adds the narrative statement that the hand of the foreigners was upon Saul.
notes.18:27: The Septuagint reads "a hundred men," matching Saul's demand in 18:25, whereas the Hebrew MT reads "two hundred men."
notes.18:28: The Greek reads "and that all Israel loved him," whereas the Hebrew MT reads "and that Michal, Saul's daughter, loved him."
notes.19:5: Greek allophylon literally means 'foreigner,' the Septuagint's regular designation for the Philistines in 1-4 Kingdoms. Unlike the Masoretic Text, the Greek makes 'all Israel' the subject of 'saw and rejoiced.'
notes.19:9: Greek katheudon reads 'sleeping' in the house, whereas the Masoretic Text reads 'sitting.'
notes.19:13: Greek kenotaphia ('cenotaphs' or funerary effigies) renders Hebrew teraphim (household idols), and hepar ton aigon reads 'a liver of goats' (also in v. 16), where the Masoretic Text has a quilt or cushion of goats' hair.
notes.19:18: The Greek distinguishes Armathaim from Ramah in the same verse, and reads Auath (also in vv. 19, 22, 23; 20:1) where the Masoretic Text reads Naioth.
notes.19:22: Greek reads 'the cistern of the threshing floor that is in Sephi' (after 'Saul was furious with anger'), where the Masoretic Text reads 'the great cistern that is in Secu.'
notes.20:3: Greek reads 'just as he said, it has been filled up between me and death,' differing from the Masoretic Text ('there is but a step between me and death').
notes.20:9: Greek reads 'and if it is not to your cities, I will report to you,' diverging from the Masoretic Text's rhetorical question ('would I not tell you?').
notes.20:16: Greek reads 'let the name of Jonathan be found from the house of David,' where the Masoretic Text reads 'so Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David.'
notes.20:19: Greek reads 'on the working day' and transliterates 'ergab' (corresponding to 'argab' in v. 41, a term for a stone mound or cairn), where the Masoretic Text reads 'on the day of the deed' and 'the stone Ezel.'
notes.20:20: Armattarei transliterates the Hebrew phrase for 'the target,' and Greek schizais (literally 'wooden shafts' or 'splinters') is used throughout this chapter for arrows.
notes.20:21: Greek gouzan is an obscure textual form or loanword referring to the arrow (called schiza in the next clause), and 'word of the Lord' reflects the Greek's extra 'of the Lord' before 'as the Lord lives.'
notes.21:2: Greek reads "Abimelech" here and throughout chs. 21-23, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Ahimelech."
notes.21:3: Greek preserves a doublet for the Hebrew idiom indicating an undisclosed place, rendering it both as a translation ("God's Faithfulness") and as a transliteration ("Phellani Maemoni").
notes.21:6: Greek frames this difficult clause as a question ("And is the journey itself common?") followed by "Because it will be sanctified today on account of my equipment" (Hebrew MT: "even though it is an ordinary journey, how much more today will their vessels be holy").
notes.21:8: "Neessaran" transliterates the Hebrew word for "detained" alongside its Greek translation; Greek also calls Doeg "the Syrian" (MT: "the Edomite") and describes him as "tending the mules of Saul" (MT: "chief of Saul's shepherds").
notes.21:10: Greek allophylos ("foreigner") is the Septuagint's regular designation for the Philistines throughout 1-2 Samuel.
notes.22:5: Greek reads "in the city of Sarik," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "in the forest of Hereth."
notes.22:6: Greek translates "Gibeah" as "the hill," renders "tamarisk tree" as "field," and reads "Bama" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Ramah."
notes.22:8: "Uncovers my ear" is a literal idiom for informing or disclosing something (also in v. 17); Greek also reads "as an enemy" here and in v. 13 (Hebrew MT: "to lie in ambush").
notes.22:18: Greek reads "three hundred and five men" (Hebrew MT: "eighty-five men") and omits "linen" before "ephod."
notes.22:23: Greek reads in the first person, "wherever I seek a place for my life, I will also seek one for your life," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "he who seeks my life seeks your life."
notes.23:2: Greek reads "you will strike Keilah," repeating the verb "strike," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "you will save Keilah."
notes.23:11: Verse 12 is absent in the Greek text; the inquiry about surrender is condensed here into the singular passive "Will it be shut up?" and answered "It will be shut up."
notes.23:13: Greek reads "about four hundred" men (consistent with 22:2), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "about six hundred."
notes.23:15: Greek Kaine (literally "New") is used as a place name here and in vv. 16, 18, and 19, corresponding to "Horesh" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.23:19: "Nessara" (like "Maserem" in v. 14) is a Greek transliteration corresponding to Hebrew "strongholds," placed here alongside the translation "in the narrow passes."
